Summarize the following news within 73 words:
UAW Targets CEO Pay During Strike
Since September, the UAW has been striking against the big three Michigan car companies, Ford, GM, and Stellantis.
The United Auto Workers are asking for better pay and more benefits.
A number of workers have walked off the job across several states. Contracts have been offered and rejected. The president and former president have visited the striking workers.
Now, the UAW has another target in their quest to win the media war.
CEO pay.
The car companies’ executives have huge compensation packages. Shawn Fawn, the UAW, said that their salaries have outpaced the workers’ wages.
Fain took to YouTube to explain his point, “They’re absolutely rolling in the money. They’re competing for who gets the biggest executive compensation package.”
According to Michigan Advance, the big three CEOs all made over $20 million. “General Motors CEO Mary Barra’s compensation is $29 million, the highest of the big three automakers, followed by Stellantis’ Carlo Tevares at $25 million and Ford’s Jim Farley at $21 million.”
Fain has been bringing up the executive officers’ salaries because they have risen by 40% since 2019 when the last contract was done. However, the auto workers' wages have only risen 6% during the same period.
Cindy Schipani, a business law professor at the University of Michigan explained how this hurts the companies during negotiations. “The union seems to be arguing an equity issue, especially in light of the sacrifices the workers needed to make in past negotiations,” she said. “Of course, the CEO’s job isn’t comparable to the job of the average worker, but I suspect the UAW may believe it has some leverage. If the company can afford to raise the salary of the top executive at roughly 40% over 4 years, why not also grant the rank and file similar increases.”

The UAW highlighted that the CEOs of the big three automakers all earned over $20m, with salaries rising by 40% since 2019, while workers' wages increased by just 6%. The union is arguing that if the companies can afford substantial executive pay raises, they should also grant similar increases for ordinary workers.

With the swell in question being generated by Super Typhoon Bolaven, their dedication to the sport was put to the ultimate test.

Initially, it was just a blip on the weather radar, slowly gaining strength as it made its way northeast.
As it passed between Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands in mid-October, it didn't appear to be anything out of the ordinary.

Bolaven underwent a meteorological transformation known as rapid intensification. In the span of a mere 12 hours, its wind speeds catapulted from around 90 mph to a jaw-dropping 160 mph, morphing it from a category one to a catastrophic category five hurricane.
At its zenith, the typhoon was unleashing winds of astonishing power, reaching speeds of up to 180 mph.
As the colossal waves generated by the force of Bolaven began their journey towards the California coast, surfers and thrill-seekers around the region knew that Maverick's was on the cusp of an unforgettable day.
Super Typhoon Bolaven may have brought havoc and destruction in its wake, but it also gifted California's most famous big wave spot with an unforgettable day of surfing.
It was a reminder that in the world of big wave riding, when the call of the ocean beckons, those who heed it are rewarded with an experience like no other.

review_info.review_text: Love their sandwiches, especially on Dutch bread! This location had a specific sandwich for SB, which is cool. Always super tasty and a lot so be prepared to share or save for another meal. Super fast service and convenient.

More so than seafood, vegetarian, or even Mexican food, the cream that rises to the top in Santa Barbara most consistently is...sandwiches! There is truly a pantheon of fine sandwich shops in our fair town and Ike's, with it's sole, somewhat squalid little location next to the 7-11 on Mission, has pushed it's way into that top tier. 

I've been there twice now and heard similar stories from friends and fam, and Ike's is the bomb. Their bread is fresh and tasty (I like the sourdough better than the Dutch Crunch, but you can't go wrong either way), the variety is hard to beat, the sauces are tasty, and they cook them oh so right. I've tried the steak sandwich and the three cheese and they were both on hit. 

Normally I'd dock a star or two for so many SF Giants references, or the weird little location, or the strange hours (closes at 6?), but the food and service are so legit that I'm not even going to go there. This spot is a legitimate contender with all the big boys in town - Valentinos, South Coast, Panino, and Sam's. Definitely worth picking up on your way to the Rose Garden or if you want to enjoy it in one of their creepy little booths staring at the weird ceiling.

The sandwiches here are awesome!  Although I despise the name of many of them (a lot of SF sports themed, while I'm an LA fan), I looked past that and enjoyed a couple sandwiches named after Giants players.  
The service was good, friendly and helpful.  Sandwiches were ready not too long after ordering them.  
The star of the sandwiches was the Dutch Crunch bread.  That is one of the most awesome breads for sandwiches, crunchy on the outside and soft interior. 
I'd definitely come back to try some of their other creations!

Here we are after following a food blogger for the past month now. First, the place has a its  own character. Old and charming in a rustic way. All raw wood, no paint. It was like a movie set. What with the bikers as main characters. We were looking forward to the foot long tri tip sandwich but I think we made a mistake ordering. What came was like a six inch tri tip sandwich! I would have loved to take a photo a loooonnnngggg sandwich much like what the food blogger had. . Now, the beef was kind of dry and I think we got the very end of the tri tip. Not as tasty or juicy as I was expecting. Next time I order, I will make sure to say that I would like the middle part of the meat and not the end.
I turned my attention to the vegetable salad and onion rings . I like the vegetable salad because the veggies were grilled and the  cranberry dressing was light and refreshing.  I wish they could have placed more.  
The onion rings  which we excitedly waited for were big and good too. We had to box the rest of it because it was too big for us.

Overall , it is a regular sandwich place in a picnic setting. Relaxed and beautiful in its simplicity. 

If you are showing friends around, I think  this is a good place to consider:

We came to this famous "old stagecoach stop turned eatery" on a cold winter day but the vibe here was super warm!   But if the vibe along isn't enough to warm your heart, the ginormous Tri-tip sandwich will certainly warm your stomach! 

The meat was done to perfection and the bun was soft... and they give you so much that the two halves of the bun hardly close!  

If you buy the $13 sandwich, you'd have to eat out in open tables. There's a restaurant but hard to get into. 

The ambiance is rustic, casual and relaxing. Parking can be difficult as this famous joint is super popular!  
CHECK THEIR HOURS before you come (they are not open every day like other restaurants) so you don't end up driving the distance and get disappointed. Lastly, my guess is this place is more enjoyable in the summertime as the shady tree-lines areas can be cold in the winter.
Although the food was good and the setting was nice. I got food poisoning after eating either the chili cheese fries or the Tavern burger.

The owner really needs to hire new people or train his employees enough to know that they're at work and not in class. 12/14/2021 I order two bagels & two hot chocolates for pickup. Important to note their hours are 11-2. I have tried on 4 different occasion to get tamales from this place.  So far my experience has been very disappointing. The first time they were sold out and closing before the 2:00 hour. The next time I went early and was in line at about 11:45 when again, they were sold out of all types but two. The next time I went at 11:10 and was told while standing in line the were sold out of everything. Keep in mind this is just a few minutes after they opened. I was able to speak with the owner and he gave me his card and said the best thing to do was to order ahead to be sure to get what I wanted. So the next day I called ahead to order for the following day.  Feeling confident I would finally have my chile and cheese tamales I was there at 11:00 only to be told they had not arrived with the tamales yet and to come back in five minutes. I did this twice more.  The woman then took my number and assured me she would call when they arrived.  I did receive a call only to inform me they had made a mistake and there were no tamales that day for me.  This business seems highly successful by the number of people lined up for their tamales however their service is slow, disorganized and inconsistent.  Every time I was in line I heard the same kind of experiences by other folks.  I would also agree with another review that these are not the best tamales and a little small for the price. The convenience of the location to my work place is the only reason I have tried so many times.  However the last time was final straw and I will not be back.

Update to this review as of 12-30-15.  Today Richard Lambert, president and I believe owner of Tamales To Go tracked me down and made a peace offering of warm tamales for the mess up on my last order.  This was very nice and a great stride in the right direction toward good customer relations.  I will give them another try in the future based on this action.

AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS TAMALES!  I've never been a huge fan of tamales - that is, until I tasted Santa Barbara Tamales To Go!  I was lucky enough to have won 12  SB Tamales at a business networking meeting.  The owner couldn't have been nicer or more accommodating.  There are 6 varieties of tamales. Overview:
response:
Santa Barbara Tamales To Go is a local Mexican restaurant located at 20 E Cota St in Santa Barbara, CA. They specialize in delicious tamales, offering a variety of flavors, including pork, chicken verde, and farmer's market. The business has received an overall rating of 4.5 stars.

Customers have mentioned that the tamales are amazingly delicious and highly recommended. They appreciate the light and fresh texture of the corn masa, as well as the perfect seasoning and flavor. One customer even won 12 tamales at a business networking meeting and enjoyed every single one of them with their friends.

However, some customers have expressed disappointment with the service at Santa Barbara Tamales To Go. They have experienced issues with the availability of tamales, with the restaurant often running out of stock, even shortly after opening. The owner has suggested ordering ahead to ensure getting the desired tamales, but there have been instances where the tamales did not arrive as promised.

Despite the service issues, the convenience of the location near the reviewer's workplace has been a motivating factor for them to try multiple times. The tamales have been described as a little small for the price, and there have been complaints about slow, disorganized, and inconsistent service.

In an effort to improve customer relations, the owner personally reached out to one customer who had a bad experience and offered them a peace offering of warm tamales. This gesture was well-received and the customer is willing to give the business another try in the future.

Overall, Santa Barbara Tamales To Go is known for their delicious tamales, but they have room for improvement in terms of service consistency and availability.

We tend to hop around to check out multiple bars to compare which ones we enjoyed the best. review_info.review_text: Shintori has the best sushi that either my wife or I have experienced in Santa Barbara!  The owners care about doing it right and taking care of there patrons. Down to asking me "How spicy do you want your spicy tuna?"  I have never had someone be that thoughtful and they were happy to accommodate. After 13 years of this being my "neighborhood" sushi place (and always busy), I finally ordered out some sushi. Delicious, fresh, great selection, reasonably priced. I can see why it is always packed. So far the best sushi I've had in Santa Barbara.

Spent $75.00 on teriyaki beef and chicken combo and it was the worst Japanese food I've ever eaten.  They put sesame leafs diced on all their rolls overpowering the sushi flavor. They also put Mexican salsa over the teriuaki beef. I owned a Japanese Restaurant before and this was the worst Japanese fusion restaurant I've ever ate. Too much jinger on everything and no teriyaki sauce on teriyaki meat.

review_info.review_text: I entered the Santa Barbara De la Vina store on 5/17 around 3 p.m. It was manned by two males. I made the mistake of bringing in my own cup to reuse. Before I could finish my sentence one of the figures asks me if I have a receipt. Now how many of you carry around a Coffee Bean receipt with you? He was under the impression I was trying to save a dollar or so. I corrected him saying I was trying to be sensitive to the environment. It was awkward. Seems like a minor thing and it is, but during the pandemic you'd think the first thing out of an employee's mouth is not asking to see my receipt and it's the only CBT store that's ever done so. BTW, they use paper straws so you'd think they'd get the environment thing.

First of all, this location is quite small and cute, and the service was p friendly!! I appreciate how they use paper straws! As a positive, they are super upfront about the nutrition of their drinks, with each item on the menu labeled with its calories. They also have lightened versions of drinks like their matcha latte if you want a lower cal option. I think this is so helpful! 
I ordered a Vietnamese cold brew, and would recommend! Not quite the authentic Vietnamese coffee you would get at other places, but pretty close! Super rich and a good source of caffeine if you need it :) Not very many interesting options on the drink menu, tho. A pretty standard coffee shop I would say.

I had such a great experience at this coffee bean and tea leaf. Christine the store manager was awesome!

review_info.review_text:
I'a used to be my go-to for seafood cravings in Santa Barbara. In a town where seafood, sandwiches, and Mexican food are the bread and butter of restaurant life, they shone. During my freshman year of college, I'd come here like clockwork to celebrate the end of another quarter with their delicious chef's special seafood cioppino and 10% student discount. Over the past two years, though, things have changed.

With the introduction of poke bowls on the menu ($12 on the laminated menus, $12.99 on the chalkboards hanging over their open kitchen), it appears that there are some new things to try at I'a since I last saw them in early 2016. I opted for a go at their shoyu salmon poke, though not entirely by my choice. Recent salmon scares (did you know fish get lice too?) made me weary of the fish, but at 5:30 p.m. on a Sunday, they were out of all but one scoop of their ahi tuna. I guess it wouldn't be as fresh as it was in the morning when prepared. 

Considering how popular of an option it was compared to the salmon bathing in spicy mayo, though, I wonder if it'd be a better restaurant practice to make more of the fish that sells. They seemed ill-prepared for any dinner rush due to the near-empty serving platters of ahi tuna and shoyru salmon, as did the guy who looked annoyed taking our orders. At the time, they also appeared to be out of octopus and hamachi.

I got a generous 3-4 scoops of salmon, which tasted slightly too fishy. My fish was swimming in way too much seaweed salad, carrots, and cucumbers, and would have been better with more bean sprouts and rice. I asked for the shoyu sauce on the side and certainly didn't regret it, since I drizzled on too much at the end and felt like I was drinking soup. Flavor-wise, it tasted like a poke salad, not a poke bowl, emphasis on the salad.

While I suppose I'm paying $12.99 for the quality, it genuinely didn't feel outstanding, and it's not like I'm paying for the ambiance either. Guess the money's going toward the service provided by the one guy who looked both bored, tired, and like he needed a beer to get through the day, and the cook running around the kitchen trying to clean and get everything else together. I'm not the fan of I'a the way I used to be, although I suppose I'll have to revisit for the fish tacos and oysters some day.

I love I'a! I am so happy that they are in the Santa Barbara Public Market. This is my go to spot for poke when I am in Downtown Santa Barbara. They have so many varieties to choose from and it is incredibly fresh. Try the Hamachi, Octopus, Spicy Salmon, Ahi Tuna...you know what, just try it all! It's wonderful. If you're taking it home, I recommend buying the poke a la carte versus in the poke bowl. It just seems you get more bang for your buck in my humble opinion. Then pair it will sauteed veggies and brown rice or cauliflower rice when you get home for a high protein, nutrition-rich meal.
Excelente servicio y ambiente. La comida espectacular. Pedimos salmón y también pulpo español. Todo muy rico, volvería sin dudarlo

source_info.name: I'a Fish Market and Cafe
source_info.categories: Poke, Seafood, American (Traditional), Specialty Food, Seafood Markets, Food, Restaurants

review_info.review_text:
I'a used to be my go-to for seafood cravings in Santa Barbara. In a town where seafood, sandwiches, and Mexican food are the bread and butter of restaurant life, they shone. During my freshman year of college, I'd come here like clockwork to celebrate the end of another quarter with their delicious chef's special seafood cioppino and 10% student discount. Over the past two years, though, things have changed.

With the introduction of poke bowls on the menu ($12 on the laminated menus, $12.99 on the chalkboards hanging over their open kitchen), it appears that there are some new things to try at I'a since I last saw them in early 2016. I opted for a go at their shoyu salmon poke, though not entirely by my choice. Recent salmon scares (did you know fish get lice too?) made me weary of the fish, but at 5:30 p.m. on a Sunday, they were out of all but one scoop of their ahi tuna. I guess it wouldn't be as fresh as it was in the morning when prepared. 

Considering how popular of an option it was compared to the salmon bathing in spicy mayo, though, I wonder if it'd be a better restaurant practice to make more of the fish that sells. They seemed ill-prepared for any dinner rush due to the near-empty serving platters of ahi tuna and shoyru salmon, as did the guy who looked annoyed taking our orders. At the time, they also appeared to be out of octopus and hamachi.

I got a generous 3-4 scoops of salmon, which tasted slightly too fishy. My fish was swimming in way too much seaweed salad, carrots, and cucumbers, and would have been better with more bean sprouts and rice. I asked for the shoyu sauce on the side and certainly didn't regret it, since I drizzled on too much at the end and felt like I was drinking soup. Flavor-wise, it tasted like a poke salad, not a poke bowl, emphasis on the salad.

While I suppose I'm paying $12.99 for the quality, it genuinely didn't feel outstanding, and it's not like I'm paying for the ambiance either. Guess the money's going toward the service provided by the one guy who looked both bored, tired, and like he needed a beer to get through the day, and the cook running around the kitchen trying to clean and get everything else together. I'm not the fan of I'a the way I used to be, although I suppose I'll have to revisit for the fish tacos and oysters some day.

I love I'a! I am so happy that they are in the Santa Barbara Public Market. This is my go to spot for poke when I am in Downtown Santa Barbara. They have so many varieties to choose from and it is incredibly fresh. Try the Hamachi, Octopus, Spicy Salmon, Ahi Tuna...you know what, just try it all! It's wonderful. If you're taking it home, I recommend buying the poke a la carte versus in the poke bowl. It just seems you get more bang for your buck in my humble opinion. Then pair it will sauteed veggies and brown rice or cauliflower rice when you get home for a high protein, nutrition-rich meal.
Excelente servicio y ambiente. La comida espectacular. Pedimos salmón y también pulpo español. Todo muy rico, volvería sin dudarlo

There was a good amount of people when we arrived at 10:00pm but around 11pm a lot of the crowd left and it wasn't too full anymore. This didn't bother us at all because well there were 8 of us and we all kept each other pretty entertained. Me and my girls seriously had one of our best nights here at M8RX and I would highly recommend this night club to anyone looking to laugh and dance the night away!

Then when I finally stayed long enough to see the guest DJ, they turned up the music waaaaay too loud. I've been to Basspod at EDC, I think this place is louder than that. it's an easy spot to grab some grub and a beer, totally casual.  There is a bit of a premium on the beer.

Darn it. I wanted to like this place so much. I did, for years. Heck, I gave them a five-star rating a mere two days prior. Can't say that I am much of a fan anymore. 

Changing my review to three stars due to the bartender's lack of service. We waited 10 minutes as he went on his phone and helped others after us. Not worth the time when there are so many other bars in Santa Barbara. We left without service.

I hope that ownership takes note of their staff's level of service and implements measures to improve upon it. A busy bar is one thing; the staff member scrolling through his phone while there are patrons waiting is a whole other level of low. You're going to lose customers!

I now understand why this venue has an average rating of three stars, not four or five. A mediocre experience overall. Regretfully, I probably will not be back.

this place is not worth the exorbitant prices and rude, inattentive bar staff. it's not hard to see when someone is sitting at the bar trying to get your attention. like... it's literally your job, not social hour. f this place

review_info.review_text: Just spoke with the owners today - they are OPEN as of today.  Our plan is to go grab dinner there tonight. I LOVE BRUMMIS.

The food is authentically German and incredibly good.  The priciest entrees are huge portions of food so really, they're quite reasonable, and there are some more affordable options as well.

I have heard that they are considering closing their doors in the next couple months so GO THERE NOW while you still can!

I could go on and on about this place.  The service is wonderful.  I highly recommend the Rouladen or Goulash (which comes with Spaetzle -- Germany's answer to mac n' cheese--- delicious).  I've heard that the various Schnitzel dishes are also extremely good.  Also, their darkest beer on tap is wunderbar.

All in all, I am heartbroken that they plan to close.  But I wish Veronika and Rudi all the best!

Brummis is a down home kind of place, nothing fancy but very comfortable. AT Brummis you get great service, a wonderful home-cooked meal and the price is perfect, just a great little place.

I order the ultimate açaí bowl and they have different size options! I always ask for extra granola. All the people that work there are also really friendly! Love this place!!

Love it so far! 
Great selection for vegans and veggies with açaí bowls and smoothies galore plus a food menu with fusion items and easy sides for those of us plain eaters! Yum! 
Lovely palm covered patio with nice lighting for night time chilling it takeout. 
Tons of tables and a good study spot for all year...

I love the shade of the vacation-vibe patio and the accessible, healthy food. The bowls are my favorite, and I adore anything with pineapple. It's good value, and I'm happy with the modest portions when I just need a quick lunch instead of leftovers for days. One evening, delivery to my apartment was so quick that I almost didn't answer the door. 

But the quality of the food varies greatly. I've had rice plates with tender beef, and rice plates with gummy sauce. I would go elsewhere for poke bowls and tacos. Hiwi excels at nourishing, vegetable-forward bowls -- brighter and more complex than Hana Kitchen. Seek those, and you'll have a guaranteed happy lunch.

review_info.review_text: I have eaten at Food Connection 3 times. The first couple experiences were great. The food was tasty and left me craving more! But last night I ate the pastor nachos and my boyfriend had the pastor burrito, and unfortunately we are both trying to recover from food poisoning. We both had pleasant experiences the first couple times, but now I don't think I can look at this food truck the same way again.

My coworkers and I stopped by here for lunch only to find the truck window closed. However, as we were leaving the owner walked up and offered to cook us something despite being closed for the day. We all ended up ordering a variety of mulitas - it was my first time trying them and they were delicious (a bit like a quesadilla but with small tortillas sandwiching the fillings); the meats and salsas were all on point. Mostly I appreciated the kindness and hospitality we received here!

source_info.categories: Food, Restaurants, Delis, Event Planning & Services, Caterers, Sandwiches

review_info.review_text:
I love pickles, so I definitely appreciate a pickles-forward sandwich shop. Three Pickles offers, true to its name, three varieties of pickles: spears, slices, and pepperoncini, all available gratis at a pickle bar, which is something I'd love to see wherever sandwiches are sold.

We met up with friends at the park the day before Thanksgiving and ordered sandwiches (and pickles) to pick up for a picnic lunch. Our friends ordered and we picked up, and both parts of the process seemed fast and easy enough.

I ordered the house sub with Italian cold cuts. The "sub our way" came on a roll with diced tomato, onion, dill pickle, olive oil, oregano, mayo, choice of mustard, and choice of cheese, with a few optional add-ons. I picked dijon and provolone and added the pepperoncini and giardiniera (both free), as well as avocado. I got the regular size, which was smaller than I expected but plenty for one meal and about right for $9.50, though the $1.99 for the pitiable amount of avocado was a rip-off. The sandwich was good, if not especially exciting, and I enjoyed it with lots of pickled pepperoncini.

I'd recommend Three Pickles if you're in the mood for a sandwich with lots of pickles. I am often in this mood, so I'll probably order from here again.
The food's good but they way overcharge on DoorDash! $14.70 For a tiny sandwich and they didn't give me the pickle pack I ordered $3.50... never again.
Just looking for a quick sandwich late lunch. Went in around 2pm on a Saturday. Quick service, place looked very clean. Rubin sandwich was delicious! Would definitely go back.

Happy 2022 everyone! This year will surely see me at Anna's quite a few more times. Checking out Anna's Bakery a few days later, I wasn't let down. 

I've sampled both the vegan glazed donut and the apple fritter, as well as the house coffee, and all were great. The donut is puffy and airy and sweet. The fritter has glorious crunchy, oily edges and a surprisingly doughy interior, complete with apple pieces and a glossy, sugary varnish. (Did you know some 'apple fritters' elsewhere don't even contain apple?) The coffee is hot and black and perfectly balances the candy-like sweetness of the baked goods. 

There's always a long line and seating is limited so be prepared. Breads and donuts and cookies are also available to go. That pink box, unmistakably brimming with tasty treats, is sure to being smiles to any gathering... especially if you have vegan friends who are so used to being left out when sweet baked goods appear.

SO friendly and donuts are always amazing. All staff, from the cashier to the owner. All lovely people. They always greet with by my name. I love to see how they interact with all customers. I am always happy to give them business as it is very well deserved. Keep up the wonderful work! Anna's has been around for a long time and has always been one of my favorites.

review_info.review_text: This "classroom" dining experience was delicious. We let the servers know that we had a show to catch and they met our timing needs. All 4 courses were excellent; expertly prepared, and the first 3 were paired with delicious wines. My favorite part of the meal was their unbelievable coconut cake with a raspberry sauce. It was spectacular. We will definitely return!!!

It had been over 20 years since we had been to the John Dunn Gourmet Dining Room. The dining room changed since we were there last. It seemed a little smaller. However, the decor was beautiful. With the sun setting, the lights in the room were enough to enjoy the look of our courses. Also, the dress code has relaxed. Back then required men were required to wear coat and slacks and women dressed up. People were in jeans and lounge wear this time while we were still dressed up. We imagined there were fewer students requesting this course, as 20 years ago, each person had their own server. While these were unexpected disappointments, the most important things have not changed........the excellent service and the excellent menu selections.

We observed the different students in the room and found one, in particular, that has been in the program for more than one semester. She was very proper and very accommodating. Our server was extremely polite and very attentive. Our water glasses were never empty until we wanted them to be. If our server was not around for some reason, someone else would step in until she returned. I could tell our server was new; so, there is nothing to say to her except to keep on learning. Her start was impressive. We wish her the best of luck in her studies. 

The food was exquisite. Before, we were able to choose between land or sea, but they have decided to go with a pre fixe menu. Unfortunately for me, two of the courses contained ingredients I do not eat. However, for the experience, I tried them. Other than the fact that those ingredients were not my favorite, I have to admit that for a short period, I enjoyed them. Each course was presented beautifully and perfectly paired with a wine. I am not a wine drinker, but I can see how people enjoy wine when properly with food. We had a five-course meal which consisted of an appetizer, a soup, a sea course, a land course, and a dessert. The first four courses were paired with a different half glass of wine. Dessert came with coffee or tea. 

When eating at the Dining Room, remember that servers are students. Some are more advanced in their studies than others. Yes, there were things that our server and other servers could have done better. However, we fully understood she is still in the process of learning. She was kind and attentive, and it showed that she was trying her best. She is well on her way to an excellent future. We definitely will return. You cannot beat the service, the food, and the price ($40 per person). Remember to give a generous tip. It goes to supporting this program.

Culinary students need a wide range of management, line, and service experience, and the John Dunn Room provides the elements of finer dining for them.
The students propose the dishes and vote for their top choices, which then become the menus. It's cool to see what they come up with. 

So, keep in mind this is a lab for them, they are learning, they are not at the top of their game yet. If you want to raise your odds of a better experience, perhaps go later in the semester. Others have noted this, and I've found that it's harder to get a reservation than earlier in the semester. 

I've been for lunch service only and it was moderately close to the beginning of the semester. I suspect that the lunch service is a lot more casual than dinner. There wasn't any crazy silverware with all the extra spoons and such, there was no crumbing the tables. 

The prices are a bargain, especially if you go for the prix fixe options that include a side salad and dessert. The choice is an omelet or a crepe as the main. I picked the crepe and was pleased with the dish. It was stuffed generously with tender spinach, sundried tomatoes and lots of chunky cream cheese, plus some salad. For dessert, a fancy layered crepe cake with pistachio brittle which I think was the highlight of the meal for everyone there. All this for $10!

There are a la carte options as well, like a soup of the day, and a selection of desserts. All at good prices, but the prix fixe is the best bang for your buck.

The interior is elegant, and for a moment you won't feel like you're at a community college. 

The clientele are mostly an older crowd, a much older crowd. Friends who work on campus report that often whole busloads of them come in from retirement homes to dine here. That's kind of awesome as an affordable fun afternoon out. The day I had lunch, there was a large party of ladies in cute purple and red hats. So this is probably popular with bookclubs too.

Service and food was okay. Mistakes were made, and we made a point to mention things in person since this is a learning space. 

Make a reservation! Always make a reservation. Parking is gnarly on campus, but I think with your reservation you can get a parking permit for the lunch hour. 

Be sure to tip - it goes into a collective bucket that provides scholarships to the culinary school.

review_info.review_text: This "classroom" dining experience was delicious. We let the servers know that we had a show to catch and they met our timing needs. All 4 courses were excellent; expertly prepared, and the first 3 were paired with delicious wines. My favorite part of the meal was their unbelievable coconut cake with a raspberry sauce. It was spectacular. We will definitely return!!!

It had been over 20 years since we had been to the John Dunn Gourmet Dining Room. The dining room changed since we were there last. It seemed a little smaller. However, the decor was beautiful. With the sun setting, the lights in the room were enough to enjoy the look of our courses. Also, the dress code has relaxed. Back then required men were required to wear coat and slacks and women dressed up. People were in jeans and lounge wear this time while we were still dressed up. We imagined there were fewer students requesting this course, as 20 years ago, each person had their own server. While these were unexpected disappointments, the most important things have not changed........the excellent service and the excellent menu selections.

We observed the different students in the room and found one, in particular, that has been in the program for more than one semester. She was very proper and very accommodating. Our server was extremely polite and very attentive. Our water glasses were never empty until we wanted them to be. If our server was not around for some reason, someone else would step in until she returned. I could tell our server was new; so, there is nothing to say to her except to keep on learning. Her start was impressive. We wish her the best of luck in her studies. 

The food was exquisite. Before, we were able to choose between land or sea, but they have decided to go with a pre fixe menu. Unfortunately for me, two of the courses contained ingredients I do not eat. However, for the experience, I tried them. Other than the fact that those ingredients were not my favorite, I have to admit that for a short period, I enjoyed them. Each course was presented beautifully and perfectly paired with a wine. I am not a wine drinker, but I can see how people enjoy wine when properly with food. We had a five-course meal which consisted of an appetizer, a soup, a sea course, a land course, and a dessert. The first four courses were paired with a different half glass of wine. Dessert came with coffee or tea. 

When eating at the Dining Room, remember that servers are students. Some are more advanced in their studies than others. Yes, there were things that our server and other servers could have done better. However, we fully understood she is still in the process of learning. She was kind and attentive, and it showed that she was trying her best. She is well on her way to an excellent future. We definitely will return. You cannot beat the service, the food, and the price ($40 per person). Remember to give a generous tip. It goes to supporting this program.

Culinary students need a wide range of management, line, and service experience, and the John Dunn Room provides the elements of finer dining for them.
The students propose the dishes and vote for their top choices, which then become the menus. It's cool to see what they come up with. 

So, keep in mind this is a lab for them, they are learning, they are not at the top of their game yet. If you want to raise your odds of a better experience, perhaps go later in the semester. Others have noted this, and I've found that it's harder to get a reservation than earlier in the semester. 

I've been for lunch service only and it was moderately close to the beginning of the semester. I suspect that the lunch service is a lot more casual than dinner. There wasn't any crazy silverware with all the extra spoons and such, there was no crumbing the tables. 

The prices are a bargain, especially if you go for the prix fixe options that include a side salad and dessert. The choice is an omelet or a crepe as the main. I picked the crepe and was pleased with the dish. It was stuffed generously with tender spinach, sundried tomatoes and lots of chunky cream cheese, plus some salad. For dessert, a fancy layered crepe cake with pistachio brittle which I think was the highlight of the meal for everyone there. All this for $10!

There are a la carte options as well, like a soup of the day, and a selection of desserts. All at good prices, but the prix fixe is the best bang for your buck.

The interior is elegant, and for a moment you won't feel like you're at a community college. 

The clientele are mostly an older crowd, a much older crowd. Friends who work on campus report that often whole busloads of them come in from retirement homes to dine here. That's kind of awesome as an affordable fun afternoon out. The day I had lunch, there was a large party of ladies in cute purple and red hats. So this is probably popular with bookclubs too.

Service and food was okay. Mistakes were made, and we made a point to mention things in person since this is a learning space. 

Make a reservation! Always make a reservation. Parking is gnarly on campus, but I think with your reservation you can get a parking permit for the lunch hour. 

Be sure to tip - it goes into a collective bucket that provides scholarships to the culinary school.

review_info.review_text:
My fiancé craves the Deep Eddy's Texas Strawberry drink and burgers from Chili's so even though I'm not a fan, I'll agree to go every once in  while. Even though I slightly dread the experience because I'd rather go to a one of a kind Santa Barbara local restaurant, this Chili's wasn't so bad. 

This time we decided to bring some friends who'd never been to a Chili's. The boys had burgers and both really liked them, but the highlight was the drink for them. The chicken tacos were a little watery and not much flavor in the beans and rice.
Our chip appetizer didn't have enough salt either, so maybe that's what was missing from the food as well.

It's the typical Chili's atmosphere, dark and cold, but very clean. It's in a great location. The waiter we had was nice and on top of it. The restaurant was not very busy so it wasn't very loud

The best part of the experience was the company, but would have much rather been to a local joint.

I got curbside to-go from here last night, and it was pretty good! We got a sirloin steak and the ancho salmon, served with steamed broccoli, Mexican rice, and awesome blossom petals. We also ordered some fried pickles and the molten chocolate cake. We both liked the fried petals and pickles - nice and crispy, and each battered differently. The broccoli was also pretty good, and a much-needed break from the saltiness of everything else. The salmon was surprisingly not too overcooked, and the steak was alright too. We really couldn't finish everything and it was very rich, so we are looking forward to eating the chocolate lava cake later today. Thankfully, they packaged the ice cream separately from the cake so it should come together well. 

The takeout experience was good, although they ran out of designated curbside to-go parking spaces. It's a popular option during the covid spike I'm sure. Staff was very nice and helpful. We don't eat at chains too often but we got a gift card here, and it was a fun sort of treat!

I went here with my friends. I ordered chili on the side, but my server told me last minute that she did not want to serve me chili because it was bad and she even mentioned that I might get salmonella. This made me feel very comfortable that my server was looking out for me-- she was practically my guardian angel despite the fact that I had a little bit of the chili on my plate and I was still charged for my chili. Overall very fun, highly recommend. Rip my toilet after too.

review_info.review_text:
My fiancé craves the Deep Eddy's Texas Strawberry drink and burgers from Chili's so even though I'm not a fan, I'll agree to go every once in  while. Even though I slightly dread the experience because I'd rather go to a one of a kind Santa Barbara local restaurant, this Chili's wasn't so bad. 

This time we decided to bring some friends who'd never been to a Chili's. The boys had burgers and both really liked them, but the highlight was the drink for them. The chicken tacos were a little watery and not much flavor in the beans and rice.
Our chip appetizer didn't have enough salt either, so maybe that's what was missing from the food as well.

It's the typical Chili's atmosphere, dark and cold, but very clean. It's in a great location. The waiter we had was nice and on top of it. The restaurant was not very busy so it wasn't very loud

The best part of the experience was the company, but would have much rather been to a local joint.

I got curbside to-go from here last night, and it was pretty good! We got a sirloin steak and the ancho salmon, served with steamed broccoli, Mexican rice, and awesome blossom petals. We also ordered some fried pickles and the molten chocolate cake. We both liked the fried petals and pickles - nice and crispy, and each battered differently. The broccoli was also pretty good, and a much-needed break from the saltiness of everything else. The salmon was surprisingly not too overcooked, and the steak was alright too. We really couldn't finish everything and it was very rich, so we are looking forward to eating the chocolate lava cake later today. Thankfully, they packaged the ice cream separately from the cake so it should come together well. 

The takeout experience was good, although they ran out of designated curbside to-go parking spaces. It's a popular option during the covid spike I'm sure. Staff was very nice and helpful. We don't eat at chains too often but we got a gift card here, and it was a fun sort of treat!

I went here with my friends. I ordered chili on the side, but my server told me last minute that she did not want to serve me chili because it was bad and she even mentioned that I might get salmonella. This made me feel very comfortable that my server was looking out for me-- she was practically my guardian angel despite the fact that I had a little bit of the chili on my plate and I was still charged for my chili. Overall very fun, highly recommend. Rip my toilet after too.

La Tapatia Bakery has been in business for over 40 years. 
The variety of Pan dulce decorates the glass shelves, my favorite being the conchas. Which do you chose, vanilla or chocolate? Both!!! You be the judge, especially when they are warm right out of the oven!!

If Pan Dulce is too sweet for you, La Tapatia also offers menudo and pozole on weekends, along with other delicious Mexican dishes which they serve on a daily basis. 
I love supporting  my neighborhood and the LatinX community, they work hard to serve Santa Barbara and Goleta county. 
Always greeting you with a smile, La Tapatia Bakery is a great choice for any craving you may have.

Best Mexican food I've found in town. There's a long line out the door for a reason. I almost don't want to leave this review because I want to keep this place for myself!  Caldo de Res, burritos, nachos (fantastic), tortes are all just delicious. It's once of those places where you really want to try other things but you're so in love with what you've already tried it makes for difficult decisions.

Would you like to pay $26 + $4 or tip for a burnt torta, two drinks and terrible presentation? Then check out La
Tapatia! $26 dollars shouldn't look like this. I'm this picture, the camarones a la diabla were around $13. Came with gummy tortillas. The flavor was there yes but the presentation was terrible. Never coming back again.

No vale la pena comer algo que está quemado y se parece mal.

source_info.categories: Restaurants, Mexican

review_info.review_text:
Its a pretty good place to have mexican food.
Its not the best but I recommend it.

I only give it one star cause its been closed for about 2 or 3 months and they change the reason for why its closed every once in a while.

Yummy and fresh food for great value . Dinner for 2 in 20 bucks - Value for money. A must go to place to eat !

I was on 10 day road trip from SF to San Dieago , with 2 day stay in santa barbara- Me and my boyfriend loved this place , it was our pick to get yummy mexican food 2 days in row. 

Tip : Try their fish tacos , Fish was well done (grilled) - they made the Healthy choce felt Yummy :)

Really solid Mexican food! They're friendly in here and clean. I had a delicious veggie burrito and didn't feel at all sick afterwards. Appreciated the mix of veggies and no cilantro :) The chips weren't warm and were a bit crispy, but I LOVED their mild salsa -- I could eat a ton of this, but I don't even love salsa! Overall an A+++ Mexican experience.

Jersey Mike's is my FAVORITE sandwich place! And the first time I tried it was this year. The taste is impeccable. 

I came to this location over summer with my friends. We sat down to eat our sandwiches. When I arrived on Thursday to pick up my sandwiches, I was met with a great attitude, a well packaged and correct order.  I hope that you properly recognize her for her commitment to your company and to us the customers.
Sincerely,
Phillip P.

This is probably the worst location I've been too. The service no matter what time of day you go is always horrible! Tried giving them another chance but this is the absolute last time I would come here.. need to hire better employees. And to make it worse the air condition is leaking.

Jersey Mike's is my FAVORITE sandwich place! And the first time I tried it was this year. The taste is impeccable. 

I came to this location over summer with my friends. We sat down to eat our sandwiches. And the nice older gentleman working the cash register just got me a cup of iced water without me asking for it. He did it out of the kindness of his heart. It was the sweetest thing ever. I will never forget it. He deserves an award. He comes up to me, gives me the water, and says, "I couldn't let you eat the sandwich without a cup of water." Awww so sweet. 

I definitely recommend this place. Get the turkey with provolone, Mike's way, and with jalapeños! Yummy :)

Good Afternoon,
I am writing in hope that Ashley Beaty of store # 20075 in Goleta California gets recognized for outstanding customer service.  I called on Monday September 27th to place a large of 25 sandwiches for my son's school.  Ashley was courteous, knowledgeable, and very professional.  She up sold on 25 bags of chips and drinks.  In a world where customer service has deteriorated into nothingness, Ashley Beaty is out there making a difference.  When I arrived on Thursday to pick up my sandwiches, I was met with a great attitude, a well packaged and correct order.  I hope that you properly recognize her for her commitment to your company and to us the customers.
Sincerely,
Phillip P.

This is probably the worst location I've been too. The service no matter what time of day you go is always horrible! Tried giving them another chance but this is the absolute last time I would come here.. need to hire better employees. And to make it worse the air condition is leaking.

review_info.review_text: Directly to the left of the Sojourner, Le Bon Cafe has been CLOSED since early February, 2008.

Directly to the left of the acclaimed Soujourner's, this little place is often overlooked. However, it is well worth a visit, especially around lunch time. Some of the food may not be particularly pleasing to the avowed meat eater, but as long as you're willing to have a healthy meal with a good dose of greens, you're in a good place. 

I remember standing in the restaurant reading a review that was posted on the wall. It mentioned something about how most patrons are avid fans of dishes that could double as as "rabbit food." I laughed. It's almost true. ALMOST being the operative word. If you're looking for a healthy meal that is delicious AND won't leave you clutching your bowels, fighting a food induced coma while feeling like you have a baby pig sleeping inside your stomach, Le Bon is the place to go.

Try the sandwiches around lunchtime - they're light, delicious, and unforgettable! Instead of opting for bread, try the carb-free option, lightly fried crushed bananas. The chef forms the banana covering into a bread-like form, and uses that instead! Get any of the sandwiches this way - I ordered the eggplant mozarella sandwich. They have a delectable pesto that adds a pleasant kick to a healthy sandwich. 

You'll leave feeling refreshed, healthy, and...(gasp) satisfied! I'm a carnivorous creature myself and usually think everything can be improved with a side of steak. However, Le Bon satisfied my leaf-eating side to the max. Now that's something, coming from someone who wants to eventually start a "Beef Depot."

I want to give this one another chance... See the thing is, I wanted to like it more than I did. The menu looks promising--I was enticed by lamb bahn mi, plaintain sandwiches, fish and chips made with sweet potato fries--but the results were just okay. That said, the vibe is great, the staff is super sweet, and they have lots of fresh salads and yummy juices. I'll definitely go back and repost once I've tried again.

review_info.review_text: Ok this place has really stepped up its game! Great customer service and friendly faces! And love the cooks! And the food ain't half bad either! Well done guys!

We were stopping off to grab Panda Express on our way home from vacation (Panda had closed early) as we were walking away dejected with two hungry children my fiancé noticed Santa Barbara Chicken Ranch tucked off to the side; I'm so glad he did! 

The cashiers were both very friendly. 

The restaurant was very clean as were the bathrooms! 

The burritos, rice and beans are large and yummy but not authentic tasting nor the best but it's a decent meal. 

Very child friendly! Except for: all of the salsas are spicy none were mild enough for my 6 yearold, but I thought they were good!

One of my coworkers brought this to lunch and it smelled really good, so I decided to give it a try. I ordered a half/half plate, with both tri-tip and chicken. Unfortunately, the plate didn't live up the my expectations. The chicken was greasy and the tri-top was bland. Neither had very good flavor. However, the beans and rice were pretty good, and the salsa was the best part of the meal, as it was full of flavor. I would maybe try here again, but order a burrito instead.

Dang....just another fart in the wind? No no- there's much more to come outta these comedians. I have a feeling this particular one may linger instead of being lost into the wind. Will I wait 1-2 for a bang burger? Does a fish swim? Ill wait as long as I can possibly wait just to chance to be a spectator to watching these guys pound their meat. Yes please.
Try there homemade Ketchup one of these guys made himself...awesome as. Well done guys! When will the C.Stain Ketchup be available in stores? My dang old lady drank the whole bottle. What's the secret ingredient? It's so familiar, I just can't put my dang finger on it. Salty yet creamy- yum! Who would a thunk it?

40 min wait after ordering and paying.  Which is frustrating because if the kitchen is that busy you owe it to customers to tell them.   

We went when they were a pop up at cork tree cellar.   You can sit anywhere inside or outside.

Prices are fair.   $13 for a double burger and fries combo.   $14 for a veggie burger  combo(better than the meat).

But after waiting all that time the burger and fries were just alright.  Nothing special at all.   Think In-n-out quality with dramatically worse fries.

The fries were what was most frustrating, as they had just brought the food out, no reason for them to be luke-warm and limp.  I would have sent them back but at that point, after 40 minutes of waiiting, we just wanted to finish up.

It would be one star probably except for the cookie.  Small but well worth the $2 indulgence at the end.

Awesome food, friendly service!

Smashburgers have become something of a trend over the past year or two - and I'm all about them. The unique way they are prepared with their crispy outer "crust" make them quite the delicacy. One issue, though - you just can't find them in greater Santa Barbara! ...or so I thought. 

I was happy to hear about Dang Burger. They are essentially a pop-up but I believe can graduate to a storefront with just how popular they've gotten. I first saw them about a few months ago on a friend's Instagram story and wow, did those burgers look delicious. I decided to follow their social media just to see where they'd be popping up. 

I have ordered from Dang three times in total (they were at Old Town Coffee tonight!). I believe they are headquartered in Carp and share a space with a wine tasting room. 

I order the same thing each time - the Dang Burger combo which I'm assuming is their flagship. Once I find an item I enjoy, it's hard to veer away and this is the current dilemma I'm facing. What a first world problem! The burger is consistently tasty with its crispy thin patty and soft bun. It's the perfect size - and the fries are the ideal complement. 

Support small and local! I look forward to coming back real soon.

If I had "accidentally" walked out with $56 worth of goods I didn't pay for i would not only have to return them all but I'd also be arrested.  Poor customer service.
I bought some fresh and organic vegetables, the price is more expensive than the supermarket, but the quality is very good.  I really like the grapefruit juice they squeezed by themselves.

review_info.review_text: Mmm I gave into my cravings once again and visited IHOP tonight. I had been thinking about the Harvest Grain Pancakes and they did not disappoint. The service was also wonderful (I was nervous reading all of the negative reviews about the service). The plate was delivered in a timely manner and the pancakes were nice and hot. Thank you for the nostalgic experience!

This place is very hidden, and nothing too exciting but I got a birthday stack of pancakes so we went in to redeem them. The pancakes had the familiar IHOP taste, and yes they were good. Surprisingly they actually looked pretty like the staged pictures on the menu, so that's impressive. Nothing to complain about regarding the pancakes.
The service was friendly and kind, but it took a while for us to be welcomed upon entering. The place was dead when we walked in and no waiters were around. Then we didn't get checked on during our meal.
It's actually a pretty spacious interior and I could see it being quite the family place on Sunday. The only other people that were there with us were ordering off the senior menu. That seems to be the crowd here.

Never again!! The waiter (in his late 50's) who took our order seemed very irritated that we were even there from the start. Coffee tasted sour and was undrinkable, when I politely asked the irritated waiter for a new coffee, that most likely sealed our fate. Our food never arrived. We noticed two groups of people who got there 20 minutes after we did receive their food which at that point it was 45minutes since we were seated so we asked our waiter for the status of our order, he didn't say one word just nodded his head and walked away. At this point I was about to get up and and leave but my gf and sister convinced me to wait. After another 25 minutes and 3 attempts to wave our waiter down (as he kept avoiding looking our way) we all decided to get up and leave. Boycotting this business from here on and you better believe im spreading the word. 0 out of 5 stars!!!

The restaurant operates from Tuesday to Saturday, between 17:00 and 21:00. The establishment offers free WiFi, outdoor seating, and allows reservations. It also provides parking in a lot, caters to group dining, and offers take-outs. 

Stella Mare's has a romantic and classy ambiance, which is appreciated by its customers. Patrons describe it as a beautiful place with a warm, upscale atmosphere, perfect for family dinners and celebrations. The restaurant's indoor greenhouse seating area is especially popular for its string lights and cozy fireplace. The service is rated excellent and the staff is noted for their accommodating nature.

review_info.review_text: Absolutely a beautiful French restaurant with history on the water. If you're dining at night, choose the greenhouse seating. They have string lights all over, making it a wonderful experience. It's still indoors, and heated so we did not feel cold even in December. The service was excellent and struck up a conversation with our waitress that also previously lived in the SF bay area. The food was excellent and pricing was so affordable. The lamb shank was near fall off the bone, and very tender and flavorful. Will return!

Such an adorable place, it reminds me of my grandmother's house with all the floral patterns, the decor is for sure very welcoming. 

We went there for a friend's birthday brunch. We were driving from LA to Santa Barbara for a day trip and were running late so we called them on our way and told them we would be 15 minutes late and they were very accommodating.

As soon as we arrived, we were welcomed by the host and taken to our table outside, it was a little cold so we asked if we could move inside and they had one table available which they set for us.

They brought us warm sourdough bread and freshly baked mini blueberry muffins, the muffins were delicious. 

I ordered the CROQUE MADAME which comes with a sunny-side-up egg, parts of the egg white were not cooked and I had to separate them, I am pretty sure I have seen it in many culinary shows that you should not serve the eggs with the white still raw. The rest of the sandwich was good. I was going to take a star away for this but we had such a pleasant experience that I decided not to.

first, we spent around 4.5 hours there and they still didn't try to throw us out! Second, the waiter was very sweet, he brought my friend a dessert with a little candle at the end that we appreciated a lot.

All in all, it was a pleasant experience and I will go back again but probably won't order the same food.

My father-in-law and his fiancée both had birthdays in November, so Matt B. and I took them out to dinner at Stella Mare's the night before Thanksgiving. It was a cold and dark out, even for our 6:15 reservation, and the restaurant was lovely, with a warm, cozily upscale atmosphere. We ate in a greenhouse room with high ceilings, tons of windows, and a fireplace. Service was good, and we enjoyed a pleasant meal. Even our 20-month-old had a swell time, though at some point, he insisted on walking around and hanging out by the fireplace. (He was mercifully well behaved, but did make eyes at the other diners.)

We started with a round of cocktails, which were pretty solid. I had a Smoky Margarita with smoky chili-infused tequila, house sweet and sour, and agave, finished with a spicy rim and a grilled lime wheel. Matt had L'Ancien, with Remy Martin cognac, Bulleit rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and Angostura and Peychaud's bitters. We switched to wine for the rest of our meal. I forget what exactly, but some kind of nice red, no complaints there.

The food was classic hearty bistro fare without much trendy flourish, ideal for dinner with grandparents, plus there was a kids' menu for our toddler--we ordered him pasta with butter and parmesan, but I think he mostly ate bread from the complimentary basket. The rest of us started with the cheese plate and deviled eggs. The cheese plate came with three unidentified but tasty cheeses, accompanied by crostini, strawberry slices, golden raisins, and some kind of fruit jam. The deviled eggs, or oeufs mimosa au homard, were quite good, supple and topped with lobster tail slices, tobiko, pickled shallots, and dill, perched on a slab of toasted French baguette over a bed of arugula and olive oil.

For our entrées, Matt and I split the canard a l'orange and the filet mignon. The duck breast was cooked a touch more than we like, but it was otherwise decent, served with parsnip purée, roasted broccoli florets, charred red wine-braised shallots, orange gastrique, candied orange zest, and pea shoots. The steak was tender and satisfying. We got it with the cognac peppercorn sauce and it came with a heap of thin fries.

Since we were celebrating, we ordered dessert. I got the lemon cake, which was light and bright, with lemon curd filling, caramelized mascarpone cream, and vanilla sauce. I also tried a bit of my father-in-law's crêpe Suzette, which was great, with housemade crêpes, Grand Marnier, orange reduction, orange segments, and powdered sugar. Matt got some McConnell's vanilla bean ice cream, which he shared with our son--baby's first hesitant taste of ice cream.

I liked Stella Mare's and would be happy to come back. It feels like a place that will be around forever, and I look forward to more family dinners in that elegant greenhouse.

review_info.review_text: Absolutely a beautiful French restaurant with history on the water. If you're dining at night, choose the greenhouse seating. They have string lights all over, making it a wonderful experience. It's still indoors, and heated so we did not feel cold even in December. The service was excellent and struck up a conversation with our waitress that also previously lived in the SF bay area. The food was excellent and pricing was so affordable. The lamb shank was near fall off the bone, and very tender and flavorful. Will return!

Such an adorable place, it reminds me of my grandmother's house with all the floral patterns, the decor is for sure very welcoming. 

We went there for a friend's birthday brunch. We were driving from LA to Santa Barbara for a day trip and were running late so we called them on our way and told them we would be 15 minutes late and they were very accommodating.

As soon as we arrived, we were welcomed by the host and taken to our table outside, it was a little cold so we asked if we could move inside and they had one table available which they set for us.

They brought us warm sourdough bread and freshly baked mini blueberry muffins, the muffins were delicious. 

I ordered the CROQUE MADAME which comes with a sunny-side-up egg, parts of the egg white were not cooked and I had to separate them, I am pretty sure I have seen it in many culinary shows that you should not serve the eggs with the white still raw. The rest of the sandwich was good. I was going to take a star away for this but we had such a pleasant experience that I decided not to.

first, we spent around 4.5 hours there and they still didn't try to throw us out! Second, the waiter was very sweet, he brought my friend a dessert with a little candle at the end that we appreciated a lot.

All in all, it was a pleasant experience and I will go back again but probably won't order the same food.

My father-in-law and his fiancée both had birthdays in November, so Matt B. and I took them out to dinner at Stella Mare's the night before Thanksgiving. It was a cold and dark out, even for our 6:15 reservation, and the restaurant was lovely, with a warm, cozily upscale atmosphere. We ate in a greenhouse room with high ceilings, tons of windows, and a fireplace. Service was good, and we enjoyed a pleasant meal. Even our 20-month-old had a swell time, though at some point, he insisted on walking around and hanging out by the fireplace. (He was mercifully well behaved, but did make eyes at the other diners.)

We started with a round of cocktails, which were pretty solid. I had a Smoky Margarita with smoky chili-infused tequila, house sweet and sour, and agave, finished with a spicy rim and a grilled lime wheel. Matt had L'Ancien, with Remy Martin cognac, Bulleit rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and Angostura and Peychaud's bitters. We switched to wine for the rest of our meal. I forget what exactly, but some kind of nice red, no complaints there.

The food was classic hearty bistro fare without much trendy flourish, ideal for dinner with grandparents, plus there was a kids' menu for our toddler--we ordered him pasta with butter and parmesan, but I think he mostly ate bread from the complimentary basket. The rest of us started with the cheese plate and deviled eggs. The cheese plate came with three unidentified but tasty cheeses, accompanied by crostini, strawberry slices, golden raisins, and some kind of fruit jam. The deviled eggs, or oeufs mimosa au homard, were quite good, supple and topped with lobster tail slices, tobiko, pickled shallots, and dill, perched on a slab of toasted French baguette over a bed of arugula and olive oil.

For our entrées, Matt and I split the canard a l'orange and the filet mignon. The duck breast was cooked a touch more than we like, but it was otherwise decent, served with parsnip purée, roasted broccoli florets, charred red wine-braised shallots, orange gastrique, candied orange zest, and pea shoots. The steak was tender and satisfying. We got it with the cognac peppercorn sauce and it came with a heap of thin fries.

Since we were celebrating, we ordered dessert. I got the lemon cake, which was light and bright, with lemon curd filling, caramelized mascarpone cream, and vanilla sauce. I also tried a bit of my father-in-law's crêpe Suzette, which was great, with housemade crêpes, Grand Marnier, orange reduction, orange segments, and powdered sugar. Matt got some McConnell's vanilla bean ice cream, which he shared with our son--baby's first hesitant taste of ice cream.

I liked Stella Mare's and would be happy to come back. It feels like a place that will be around forever, and I look forward to more family dinners in that elegant greenhouse.

My father-in-law and his fiancée both had birthdays in November, so Matt B. and I took them out to dinner at Stella Mare's the night before Thanksgiving. It was a cold and dark out, even for our 6:15 reservation, and the restaurant was lovely, with a warm, cozily upscale atmosphere. We ate in a greenhouse room with high ceilings, tons of windows, and a fireplace. Service was good, and we enjoyed a pleasant meal. Even our 20-month-old had a swell time, though at some point, he insisted on walking around and hanging out by the fireplace. (He was mercifully well behaved, but did make eyes at the other diners.)

We started with a round of cocktails, which were pretty solid. I had a Smoky Margarita with smoky chili-infused tequila, house sweet and sour, and agave, finished with a spicy rim and a grilled lime wheel. Matt had L'Ancien, with Remy Martin cognac, Bulleit rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and Angostura and Peychaud's bitters. We switched to wine for the rest of our meal. I forget what exactly, but some kind of nice red, no complaints there.

The food was classic hearty bistro fare without much trendy flourish, ideal for dinner with grandparents, plus there was a kids' menu for our toddler--we ordered him pasta with butter and parmesan, but I think he mostly ate bread from the complimentary basket. The rest of us started with the cheese plate and deviled eggs. The cheese plate came with three unidentified but tasty cheeses, accompanied by crostini, strawberry slices, golden raisins, and some kind of fruit jam. The deviled eggs, or oeufs mimosa au homard, were quite good, supple and topped with lobster tail slices, tobiko, pickled shallots, and dill, perched on a slab of toasted French baguette over a bed of arugula and olive oil.

For our entrées, Matt and I split the canard a l'orange and the filet mignon. The duck breast was cooked a touch more than we like, but it was otherwise decent, served with parsnip purée, roasted broccoli florets, charred red wine-braised shallots, orange gastrique, candied orange zest, and pea shoots. The steak was tender and satisfying. We got it with the cognac peppercorn sauce and it came with a heap of thin fries.

Since we were celebrating, we ordered dessert. I got the lemon cake, which was light and bright, with lemon curd filling, caramelized mascarpone cream, and vanilla sauce. I also tried a bit of my father-in-law's crêpe Suzette, which was great, with housemade crêpes, Grand Marnier, orange reduction, orange segments, and powdered sugar. Matt got some McConnell's vanilla bean ice cream, which he shared with our son--baby's first hesitant taste of ice cream.

I liked Stella Mare's and would be happy to come back. It feels like a place that will be around forever, and I look forward to more family dinners in that elegant greenhouse.

Overall, Gino's Sicilian Express is a great option for those looking for delicious and authentic Italian cuisine in a cozy and welcoming environment. The restaurant's excellent service, tasty food, and prime location make it a popular spot for both locals and visitors to Santa Barbara.

Oh man, I love the Energy Burrito with chicken here. It's probably the furthest from authentic you can get, but authenticity doesn't have a monopoly on delicious! I like it so much I simply haven't tried the other options, though I hear they're good (and pretty authentic). 

I would say the consistency isn't the best - sometimes it's a bland or weirdly dry or otherwise "off," but when they do it right it's my second favorite burrito. Love to let the juice from the burrito run onto the tortilla chips that come with...

I would go here again but I would stick with a simple chicken taco and nothing that sounds greasy.  The shrimp quesadilla was just too much cheese and greasy.  If that's what you're into then you'll love it.  Probably not the best food choice if you're at all health conscious.  But if you order smart you'll be just fine.  The food is good.  The salsa bar is exceptional.  Fresh everything to suit anyone's needs for whatever plate you order.  You can order a Mexican beer here to go with your meal which is always a plus.  I would recommend, but watch what you order.

Energy burrito - whole wheat tortilla, grilled chicken, jack cheese & romaine lettuce. 

Honestly, the burrito was only okay. If it were for the guacamole sauce, I wouldn't have like it one bit. The chicken was quite spicy (even though it didn't say it was suppose to be spicy) & there wasn't enough romaine lettuce in my opinion. However, each order does come with a side of tortilla chips & the burritos are definitely big enough to feed two!

review_info.review_text:
Oh man, I love the Energy Burrito with chicken here. It's probably the furthest from authentic you can get, but authenticity doesn't have a monopoly on delicious! I like it so much I simply haven't tried the other options, though I hear they're good (and pretty authentic). 

I would say the consistency isn't the best - sometimes it's a bland or weirdly dry or otherwise "off," but when they do it right it's my second favorite burrito. Love to let the juice from the burrito run onto the tortilla chips that come with...

I would go here again but I would stick with a simple chicken taco and nothing that sounds greasy.  The shrimp quesadilla was just too much cheese and greasy.  If that's what you're into then you'll love it.  Probably not the best food choice if you're at all health conscious.  But if you order smart you'll be just fine.  The food is good.  The salsa bar is exceptional.  Fresh everything to suit anyone's needs for whatever plate you order.  You can order a Mexican beer here to go with your meal which is always a plus.  I would recommend, but watch what you order.

Energy burrito - whole wheat tortilla, grilled chicken, jack cheese & romaine lettuce. 

Honestly, the burrito was only okay. If it were for the guacamole sauce, I wouldn't have like it one bit. The chicken was quite spicy (even though it didn't say it was suppose to be spicy) & there wasn't enough romaine lettuce in my opinion. However, each order does come with a side of tortilla chips & the burritos are definitely big enough to feed two!

review_info.review_text: We almost gave this place a pass - not a lot of upfront charm. But the Yelp reviews were good so we gave it a try. Glad we did! Friendly service as soon as we walked in. Basic breakfast was hot and delicious. I had scrambled eggs (fresh and yummy) with crispy hash browns and sourdough toast. My husband had the veggie scramble (zucchini, red peppers, onion, mushrooms) all fresh and delicious, with the same sides I had. Good cup of coffee, also! We appreciate a hard-working local restaurant and will definitely come back. Four stars just because the ambiance isn't really there. Don't let that stop you from giving this place a try!

We were coming home from a college visit trip to SLO and UCSB and wanted to hit Carp for breakfast. My kid typed in breakfast and this was one of the first that popped up - thank you Yelp!! Mom and pop-type small strip-mall cafe and we loved it. My wife and kids had pancakes (wife added blueberries) with eggs and I had the French toast. A side of hash browns to share (although we probably didn't need it) - just what the road trip ordered. Super friendly and when the people in front of us didn't need menus because the locals know what they want, it is a good sign. Hard working family, but open from 7am-2pm so it might not be a bad gig.... We will stop there again I am sure.

Hugo's Restaurant in Carpinteria is THE best breakfast/brunch spot. I especially love their pancakes, stir fried noodles, and chilaquiles! Their menu is so diverse and anyone can find something to their liking. 

The owners are so welcoming and joyful every time I visit. They have been operating for 20+ years! The service is phenomenal; you never have to wait long for your food. 

If you're ever in the area, this is the spot.

review_info.review_text: I've been going to Don Q for 40+ years! While other pool halls have come and gone, Don Q has endured - I think they still have the same 70s-80s rock playlist in the jukebox. They have the highest quality tables and cloth, both bar and regulation size. It's fun and comfortable with the kids, a date, your wife or the guys - never feels seedy or uncomfortable. The beer and snack selection have increased greatly over time, and are downright over the top now. My only wishes: that they still had scoring beads for straight pool, some chalk cones, and didn't require the felt pad under the cue ball at break. Nonetheless, Don Q is the absolute best place to play pool in SB.

this place is not a real billiards hall. the felt on all the pool tables is in  bad shape & when u ask the owner about it he'll just be rude.! stiix in ventura is where u have to go to play on real billiards tables. the only reason they r still open is because the kids know they can drink there !

The management at Don Q is probably the worst we've ever encountered in any business venue. We visited there after speaking to someone over the phone to discuss a possible opportunity for a large party event. The venue was relatively full but not overwhelming and the individual in charge couldn't take even a minute to talk to us complaining he was too busy; and, he even avoided us even though we waited for a possible 5 minutes of his time. 

Along side this extreme rudeness, the venue allows outside food to be brought in. It wreaked of uncovered food throughout the place. Food on every counter and bar stool. Quite gross. 

I have to say I will never visit Don Q's again. Management is the rudest I've ever encountered and the place smells. They have a lot to learn about running a business and they missed out on a lucrative opportunity.
