review_info.review_text: I came here for a quick drink on a Friday night. It was such a nice little rooftop bar on top of the Hilton hotel in Goleta! The atmosphere was nice. There was plenty of seating and a fireplace on each side of the rooftop. The bar was fully stocked and had 3 TVs. They had a good food menu but I only ended up ordering chicken wings. I ordered the Paloma drink which tasted good and a little strong, just the way I like!

Rooftop bistro and Bar with great Mountain View in search of decent management. We stopped in to attend a gathering for a co workers retirement. The rooftop is spacious with a couple fireplaces and some sofas. It was a great place to relax, have a drink and still be able to move around and visit.  Drinks were ok and food was average for the prices. Erin our server was efficient, friendly and did a fabulous job waiting on us. 
However, that is where we have to end our compliments. 
I could not give more than one star due to the management of this Bistro. Victor Cortez approached us with an attitude from the minute we arrived and although I understand businesses need some policies let's listen to our customer base and evaluate situations. We did have reservations for a large group. We could not split the bill in anyway, it all had to be tallied together and paid with one credit card. 
This makes things very difficult with a large number of coworkers and people arriving at different times. Our coworker also brought a retirement cake and was informed by Victor that (we don't do cakes) and if you expect to have that cake it will be an extra charge of $4 a person. Victor also told one of our party they should leave immediately when they tried to approach him to discuss the situation. 
All of us at this gathering work in the service industry and have dealt with many customers. We were all appalled at the lack of effective management and his lack of management training. Because of this I cannot recommend this place for any party over two and not sure if anyone should come back here. 
What I discovered here:  although a great rooftop with an awesome Mountain View it turns out to be just another mediocre poorly managed hotel bar.

We had made reservations for a group of 15+ to celebrate a friends retirement at the Roof Top Bistro and Bar. Speaking with friends we agreed that this restaurant /bar would be a great venue due to the open space, good food and drinks, and how accommodating the staff have  always been for other gatherings we've had there.

As I was setting up by the fireplace I was approached by the manager, and was  informed that our reservation was set up at a specific table. I asked if we can switch it so we can have the fireplace. He informed me that the area I was requesting cannot  accommodate 15+ people. I agreed but asked if we can still be sat by the fireplace. He begrudgingly agreed and noticed I was setting up to display a cake for the celebrant. He for some reason was annoyed at me from the get go but when he laid eyes on the cake he turned it up a notch.

He informed me that there was a $4/person charge for the cake if we were to plate and serve it at this establishment. I told him I was unaware of this rule since I've thrown a baby shower at this Bistro in the past and had not been charged the cake  fee. 

But, wow, just wow! Victor Cortez needs a lesson in customer service. I appreciate rules and sticking to them, but to throw attitude is uncalled for. I work in a service industry, I'm a nurse. If I treated my patients the was he did me and my friends I would be fired. The only light to my interaction with Victor was our attentive and wonderful waitress, Erin. She is a true gem and handled herself gracefully with our large group.

After being closed for 14 months, I would've thought he would be appreciative having the restaurant open. No, not Victor. I felt as if I was putting him out. So the 2 stars goes to Victor.

review_info.review_text: So sad to hear Muddy's is closing . Great coffee house, eclectic art and people! Not sure where my go to place will be now......

So many little spaces, rooms, and nooks to sit on a chair, couch or table.  Perfect for working, meeting up with friends, hanging out.  Great inside and outside space.  Art focused, which I LOVE!

If I lived closer, this would be a regular spot.

Decent coffee at an okay price. Some people like the decorations but I thought it was kind of messy and had a grandma-esque vibe too it. 

I got my usual, an iced coffee and HOT DAMN. It was strong...like a too strong for my tastes. I will come back to try their other drinks though. Not giving up on this place just yet!

review_info.review_text: I consider myself a patient person but this place made me lose my mind. Not to mention the food was a total disappointment. Ants on the wall, rude waiter, and dirty to go boxes. OH! And I wasn't served my complimentary chips. I ordered a bean and cheese (wet burrito) and it was served warm borderline cold. The beans and enchilada sauce were probably canned... at least that's what it tasted like. The tortilla was chewy (and not in a good way) . If you're not from carp and want Mexican food I suggest walk past this place.

The wife and I have frequented this restaurant a few times before, so we're familiar with the food, or so we thought. We ate at this restaurant on Friday, September 10th. 

My wife will only eat chicken breast. Boneless and skinless. She doesn't eat thighs, drumsticks,  or wings. Nope. Ain't happening. 

She ordered the hard shell tacos with chicken breast. I  ordered the mole negro, one of my favorite dishes. It was a dish my mom used to make for me.

As we started to eat I could see my wife's face. She didn't seem to be enjoying her meal.  I asked her what was wrong. The tacos were made with thigh meat. Ruined her meal, which ended up being rice & beans, chips and salsa.

As I  continued to eat my mole I noticed that the chicken didn't taste right. Mole has a strong flavor but I noticed that the chicken squares tasted a little "tangy". 

I ate about half of it but ended doing the same as the wife and only ate the rice and beans with chips and salsa. 

We walked to the restaurant and not even halfway to our place my body started to let me know it wasn't happy. I ended up being sick until this afternoon  (buuuuurrrpp!!). Excuse me. *cue sour, gross aftertaste*

Thanks for ruining my vacation.

Very slow service and lots of mistakes. Not much organization. They bring out the wrong food, two waiters keep asking us for drinks or for our order not knowing them at the other person just did. The food is so-so also.

I wanted to give this restaurant a try and I wasn't disappointed. The server greeted me and asked if I wanted to select the buffet as an option or a la carte. A la carte was my choice and I ordered something familiar "sweet an sour chicken" which wouldn't disappoint me. 

The arrival time of my order was approx. 12 minutes. I was served with a pot of rice and a plenty of sweet and sour chicken that I could not finish the dish even though I tried my hardest lol.

What I most appreciated about the staff was their composure and time they had given me to enjoy my meal without the extra "are you finished" and the constant hovering near my dining table. I like their relaxed demeanor.

Stopped by for a hunting trip. This restaurant hosting a buffet and a regular order restaurant. When first entered , we see greeted by a kitchen worker. Then the owner came out and served us. We ordered about 7 plates. No pictures. 

1. Taste: all the food we ordered were just standard Chinese good and does not required any sophisticated skill. All the food we ordered tastes way way way lower than all other restaurants. Trufully my 2 year old son cooks much much better than this. 0 star
2. Service:after the initial encounter with the kitchen worker then the service started receiving some service. 2star
3. Hygiene: this is considered pretty clean and neat restaurant. 4 star
4. Quality: kind of bad. The chicken we ordered were too old and dried. The soup, we're just MSG water and some fish balls in it. The water were tape water.  The tomato fried eggs( eggs over cooked tomato too raw). 1 star

BUFFET ONLY REVIEW 
Food was dry and flavorless , barely any options . Tasted worse than most take out Chinese places. You could taste how old the food was it looked like it was sitting out for about three to four hours. No ice cream or any decent deserts either besides jello. DO NOT EAT AT THE BUFFET.

review_info.review_text:
Matt B. and I spent Thanksgiving week at his dad's in Montecito, and on the Wednesday night in the cold and dark, we decided to walk to the Miramar for a nightcap. This wasn't our first time drinking at the hotel--we've been to the oceanfront bars a couple times, where we feel like we're getting the view/atmosphere/Rosewood experience for the relatively affordable price of two unreasonably expensive, mediocre cocktails. The Manor Bar doesn't come with views of the water, but it is an exceedingly lovely hotel bar and the cocktails are actually good.

We walked in around 10:00 the night before Thanksgiving, and the place was calm but not empty, which felt ideal. It was beautiful and cozy in a cigars-and-whiskey lounge kind of way, with dark wood paneling, intricate ceiling work, a fireplace, and leather and plush fabric furniture. We sat at the bar, which was very attractive, and ordered a round of drinks from a friendly, formally dressed bartender.

All the cocktails were named for books--a cute touch--and we got A Game of Thrones and a Catch-22. A Game of Thrones was a scotch drink with Glenmorangie 10 yr, Talisker 10 yr, lemon, citrus oleo saccharum, and egg white. An excellent cocktail, smoky and bright with a nice creamy froth on top. The Catch-22 was balanced and boozy, with Hennessy VSOP, Whistle Pig 10 yr, Dolin Rouge, and Benedictine.

We noticed a smoking cloche behind the bar and talked to the bartender about what it was used for, apparently a cocktail that wasn't on the current menu (but which he seemed perfectly able and ready to make). Maybe we'll try it next time we're at the Manor Bar. I suspect we'll make the walk over whenever we're in town.

A wonderful wood paneled clubby bar in the Rosewood Miramar this is a nearly perfect spot to enjoy fireside drinks and (at times) music. While we have come for years, I removed one star as the vast collection of dirty glasses on the bar top has somehow become a signature of the space. Also the food menu was better when the resort first opened with Caruso's Rigatoni being a beloved dish. Staff are kind, thoughtful if not all polished.

Best bartender super friendly and knowledgeable. I asked for a super complicated cocktail that was on the menu 3 years ago and made it in a jiffy. Love the live music and the vibe. Would come back any day

review_info.review_text:
Matt B. and I spent Thanksgiving week at his dad's in Montecito, and on the Wednesday night in the cold and dark, we decided to walk to the Miramar for a nightcap. This wasn't our first time drinking at the hotel--we've been to the oceanfront bars a couple times, where we feel like we're getting the view/atmosphere/Rosewood experience for the relatively affordable price of two unreasonably expensive, mediocre cocktails. The Manor Bar doesn't come with views of the water, but it is an exceedingly lovely hotel bar and the cocktails are actually good.

We walked in around 10:00 the night before Thanksgiving, and the place was calm but not empty, which felt ideal. It was beautiful and cozy in a cigars-and-whiskey lounge kind of way, with dark wood paneling, intricate ceiling work, a fireplace, and leather and plush fabric furniture. We sat at the bar, which was very attractive, and ordered a round of drinks from a friendly, formally dressed bartender.

All the cocktails were named for books--a cute touch--and we got A Game of Thrones and a Catch-22. A Game of Thrones was a scotch drink with Glenmorangie 10 yr, Talisker 10 yr, lemon, citrus oleo saccharum, and egg white. An excellent cocktail, smoky and bright with a nice creamy froth on top. The Catch-22 was balanced and boozy, with Hennessy VSOP, Whistle Pig 10 yr, Dolin Rouge, and Benedictine.

We noticed a smoking cloche behind the bar and talked to the bartender about what it was used for, apparently a cocktail that wasn't on the current menu (but which he seemed perfectly able and ready to make). Maybe we'll try it next time we're at the Manor Bar. I suspect we'll make the walk over whenever we're in town.

A wonderful wood paneled clubby bar in the Rosewood Miramar this is a nearly perfect spot to enjoy fireside drinks and (at times) music. While we have come for years, I removed one star as the vast collection of dirty glasses on the bar top has somehow become a signature of the space. Also the food menu was better when the resort first opened with Caruso's Rigatoni being a beloved dish. Staff are kind, thoughtful if not all polished.

Best bartender super friendly and knowledgeable. I asked for a super complicated cocktail that was on the menu 3 years ago and made it in a jiffy. Love the live music and the vibe. Would come back any day

review_info.review_text:
This place makes you  have a good time...

A friend recommended this bar/club for my friend and I to go to when we went to SB because we wanted to experience SB's nightlife. We got there around 9:30pm, and it wasn't crowded yet...so we got a good spot at the bar and ordered a drink...the drinks are decently priced...beers around 6-7 bucks, mixed drinks about 9 bucks. The bar tender even gave my friend a free drink! Awesome!

The dancefloor didn't have people dancing on it until about 10:30pm, but from then on people were having fun! There were some guys that all they wanted to do was rub up against you...but that's to be expected. 

When my friend and I got tired of dancing, we went up to the 2nd floor where they have private lounge areas, which was sweet...it gives you time to cool down before you head back to your hotel. They have a bar on the 2nd floor too if you want more to drink.

Overall, we had a fun night...and I think everyone should stop by this bar when they're in SB.

We had a fun time playing pool and eating California rolls at Q's. When we go down to Santa Barbara we spend alot of time eating, drinking, and walking the town.  This place gave us another option (playing pool). 

Unfortunately when we were down in March we missed it but look forward to visiting again next time.

Okay when I first started going here every thurs and some other nights I would have given it a 4-5 but now a 3. 

1. Bars: A definite plus! They have 4 bars total. One on each floor and one outside. The drinks are nice and stiff, make friends with the bartenders and they give you discounts. All are super nice. The drinks are pretty average, about $5-10. I like the seven and sevens, the black label and cokes, the midori sours, washington apple shots, long islands etc etc. 

2. Dance floor way too small for how many ppl come here, no matter the night. But mostly Thursdays and Saturdays. It just gets crowded and you have ppl glaring at you and not dancing but they're on the dance floor. Uhhhh don't get that.

3. Crowd: It has a mix, but definitely some older guys will come here on Thurs. college night to hit on the youngins. However, you can always get a free drink! LOL Definite older crowd on other nights. And 80's night Tuesdays. Just be careful of the creepers ladies, they are there watching you! HA! no joke!

In the beginning I definitely had tons of fun meeting new people and seeing all my friends from SB but now they have 18+ on Thursday nights. NO THANKS! Its not like its not crowded enough! I'll have to admit how much trouble I got in when I go here! The drinks and just everything combined you can't help but get all crazy!

4. First Floor: There are seating outside in a smoking patio,a bar. Theres seating inside on the sides of the bar, tables, huge bar and dance floor, bathroom. The basics.

5. Second Floor: Small, VIP sectioned off, a tiny bar, bathroom, can ppl watch down below which is fun sometimes. No seating unless in "VIP" area.

6. Third Floor: Pool tables galore. They have about 5 I think. They also have another bar, a bathroom and really comfy couches that I would sleep on. :D Fair warning if you're about to crash don't sit there b/c you won't get up. LOL

This holds a place in my heart b/c I've had so many crazy memories here. However, I just do not like the changes I have seen. i.e. 18+ and the mere fact that I got over the dance floor. Too crowded that it pushed me away. :(

O and for those who get SUPER drunk and can't walk, be forewarned they will kick you out! :D aka my housemate LOL

Also a thank you shout  out to the staff like Carly. You can appreciate her smile through her eyes. They really know service even though you order and usually pick it up at the counter, but they will bring it to you as well sometimes. 

They've got a lot of super food lattes. There's outdoor seating and shade or sun. They leave the doors open so there's good airflow. And there's also wonderful shirts on the wall honoring first responders and celebrating different fire stations.

review_info.review_text: We got married at the university club/ Riviera Mansion October 2021- and it truly couldn't have been a more perfect venue! The day felt completely magical, the staff was incredible, professional, and helpful, and the packages they offer make planning so simple. For anyone looking for a venue in Santa Barbara, I'd 10/10 recommend this place!

Came here for lunch with my Aunt who is a member.  We sat on the gorgeous patio.   Excellent options on the menu - something for everyone.  The service is IMPECCABLE.  I got there early and was treated like a valued guest.  I was there on free glass of wine day - the wine was wonderful.  I ordered the French Dip sandwich. Food is really good, but service here and ambiance is five star all day long.

The Riviera Mansion was the first wedding venue we looked at and the one we ended up falling for. We loved that it had the option of indoor/outdoor spaces and that we could have the entire venue to ourselves for the day. It was the perfect size to accommodate our 100 guests comfortably. The mansion and the grounds were a beautiful backdrop for all of our photos as well. Breanna was very responsive to all of our questions and was so great to work with. Chef Jamie was also nice enough to help us create a menu that met our needs and was present at our tasting to meet with us. Very pleased with our choice!!

Came here for lunch with my Aunt who is a member.  We sat on the gorgeous patio.   Excellent options on the menu - something for everyone.  The service is IMPECCABLE.  I got there early and was treated like a valued guest.  I was there on free glass of wine day - the wine was wonderful.  I ordered the French Dip sandwich. My cousin ordered the fresh ahi and my aunt had the soup.  Generous servings.  Again, our waiter and waitress made this such a wonderful afternoon. The mansion and the grounds were a beautiful backdrop for all of our photos as well. Breanna was very responsive to all of our questions and was so great to work with. Chef Jamie was also nice enough to help us create a menu that met our needs and was present at our tasting to meet with us. Very pleased with our choice!!

review_info.review_text: I eat at the Natural Cafe quite often. The food is fresh and it's easy for me to get take out. The staff is generally very friendly and I appreciate the food choices. Today, I ordered a half an old town salad to go with Sautéed tofu. Everything was there, but as I began eating it, a rather large winged bug crawled out of the lettuce. It concerns me that the lettuce and vegetables are not being washed properly, particularly in a time when people are so worried about illness.  It seems just recently that I have noticed this sort of thing happening.  I think cleanliness is of the utmost concern at this time. I hope the issue is resolved. Thank you.

fast, tasty, reasonably priced... seriously can't get any better! This food hits the spot! the portions are great, definitely get what you pay for, AND the food is so so tasty and good for ya! we couldn't have asked for more! we recommend the mexican inspired food! burritos, enchiladas, and tacos are all so fresh and good! but also can't go wrong with any of the vegetarian stir fry or sand which options!

Probably one of my faves in all of Santa Barbara. While there isn't table service (you order at the counter), the finished product of food entree is usually a work of art.

I ordered a shredded burrito & beer one afternoon upon leaving SB, and needed something to stay on my bones for a while when driving eastbound into Pasadena. review_info.review_text: I eat at the Natural Cafe quite often. The food is fresh and it's easy for me to get take out. The staff is generally very friendly and I appreciate the food choices. Today, I ordered a half an old town salad to go with Sautéed tofu. Everything was there, but as I began eating it, a rather large winged bug crawled out of the lettuce. It concerns me that the lettuce and vegetables are not being washed properly, particularly in a time when people are so worried about illness.  It seems just recently that I have noticed this sort of thing happening.  I think cleanliness is of the utmost concern at this time. I hope the issue is resolved. Thank you.

fast, tasty, reasonably priced... seriously can't get any better! This food hits the spot! the portions are great, definitely get what you pay for, AND the food is so so tasty and good for ya! we couldn't have asked for more! we recommend the mexican inspired food! burritos, enchiladas, and tacos are all so fresh and good! but also can't go wrong with any of the vegetarian stir fry or sand which options!

Probably one of my faves in all of Santa Barbara. While there isn't table service (you order at the counter), the finished product of food entree is usually a work of art.

I ordered a shredded burrito & beer one afternoon upon leaving SB, and needed something to stay on my bones for a while when driving eastbound into Pasadena. Natural Cafe served up an entree that was a pleasant surprise, with shredded beef that seemed lightly seasoned. Even the salad was pretty good. No complaints about the beer.

It took a little time for the burrito to arrive, which was ok. I had eaten one of the cookies sold at the counter as a small appetizer. While an employee indicated that there was Wi-Fi, this really isn't set up for it. I had taken a tablet out to reference something, yet had to use my network. No big deal.

I love returning to this venue, and highly recommend it for a good lunch.

review_info.review_text:
Ate with party of nine, which group they could not seat in one place, so broke into groups of 5 an 4. OK, our bad, only so many seats and booths, no reservation. I had the broiled salmon. Fairly small piece, very thin, but tasty, offered with carrots, which I did not want, substituted cole slaw, which was good, Also served with home fries, which were good. Spouse had Beef Stroganov. Rated it 'OK' also served with carrots, not a fav. Two had corned beef and cabbage, rated it good, and took some home. One complained the cabbage wasn't properly done. Another had pork chops; tasted OK but were very thin, a little dry. 
Didn't get reports from the other table. In my view the food was OK, not memorable. My Salmon dinner was over-priced at $33. Heck of a better deal at Pepe's Mexican at $15.95, bigger piece of fish, Chile Relleno and with a better side and fruit salsa. And the carrots? No broccoli, no green beans just boiled carrots the only veggie?. 
The only plus was a great server - sorry I didn't get her name.

Traditional Coffee Shop, it looks like a Denny's and the food is comparable. A little on the bland and greasy side of the aisle. I ordered Cinnamon Raisin French Toast and hashbrowns.

French Toast - came out flat and mushy.
Hashbrowns with cheese - greasy and only crisp on top.

Coffee was good and service was pleasant. 

Not worth a stop in my opinion!

Waitress is the only reason this place gets any stars! For 2 adults and a child it was $60! We could've gone to a steakhouse. The food was crap- soggy hashbrowns, chewy pancakes, watery coffee. Skip this place!

review_info.review_text:
Wanted to have a great experience here when they reopened but it was pretty ok. 

We arrived and we're seated quickly which was great and they accommodated getting us in a spot where a baby car seat could easily fit next to our table outside. 

The menu seems to be a lot smaller and different than the previous menu at the project which we were bummed about. 

When our waiter first came over I let them know I had a few dietary restrictions, he seemed unsure about how to answer my questions so bc of his uncertainties he just said I shouldn't order basically anything. When I asked him to check with the kitchen he initially said no. After much pressing on this he finally went back and asked. I learned that the blue corn tortillas (which are gluten free at corazon) are not gluten free at the project. When he finally asked the kitchen they let him know they did have some pre made gluten free corn tortillas on hand that they could use to make a taco. It always is odd to me when restaurants make corn tortillas which are traditionally gluten free with gluten, this should be more clearly identified on a menu and staff should be more knowledgeable and willing to accommodate. 

Once we finally got through the pain of ordering with our waiter we got our appetizer. We ordered the "avocado" which we assumed would be chips and guac. It was a little different but was delicious! The avocado dip had some sort of different season in it which made it delightful, would definitely recommend this! 

As for the tacos, we all thought the old project menu had better options and decided we'd prefer to just get the tacos at corazon as we thought they are ultimately better.

Love the fun vibe of the project, but we'll keep going to Corazon at public market where they have everything down to an art and customer service seems to be be more on par.

Went here for dinner and had the steak and fries, as well as the mussels and clams. The steak had a chimichurri sauce that really overpowered the whole plate. I left most of it because of the overpowering taste, and it was not tender. The mussels and clams were pretty good, but not great (maybe a 3.5 out of 5 review, for that plate). The restaurant wasn't too busy and we never got a water refill. 2 stars for the pricey chewy steak  and subpar service.
This was exceptional Mexican food. Wonderful, complex flavors that I never experienced before. A real treat.

Overview:
response:
The Project -- Corazón Cocina & Taproom is a local business located at 214 State St in Santa Barbara, CA. It offers a variety of services including breweries, bars, burgers, Mexican cuisine, tacos, cocktail bars, club crawl, breakfast & brunch, beer bar, nightlife, restaurants, and food. The business has received an average rating of 4.0 stars.

Customers have left reviews regarding their experiences at The Project -- Corazón Cocina & Taproom. One customer mentioned that they had a decent experience when they visited. They appreciated the quick seating and the accommodation of a baby car seat at their outdoor table. However, they were disappointed with the smaller and different menu compared to the previous menu at The Project. The customer also had dietary restrictions and faced challenges with the waiter's knowledge and willingness to accommodate them. Despite these issues, they enjoyed the avocado dip and recommended it. They felt that the tacos at Corazon were ultimately better and preferred to go there for their taco fix.

Another customer had a less satisfactory experience. They ordered the steak and fries, as well as the mussels and clams. The chimichurri sauce on the steak was overpowering and the steak itself was not tender. The mussels and clams were decent but not exceptional. The customer also noted subpar service, as they never received a water refill.

On a positive note, one customer described the Mexican food at The Project -- Corazón Cocina & Taproom as exceptional, with wonderful and complex flavors that they had never experienced before.

Overall, The Project -- Corazón Cocina & Taproom offers a range of services and has received mixed reviews from customers.

review_info.review_text:
Wanted to have a great experience here when they reopened but it was pretty ok. 

We arrived and we're seated quickly which was great and they accommodated getting us in a spot where a baby car seat could easily fit next to our table outside. 

The menu seems to be a lot smaller and different than the previous menu at the project which we were bummed about. 

When our waiter first came over I let them know I had a few dietary restrictions, he seemed unsure about how to answer my questions so bc of his uncertainties he just said I shouldn't order basically anything. When I asked him to check with the kitchen he initially said no. After much pressing on this he finally went back and asked. I learned that the blue corn tortillas (which are gluten free at corazon) are not gluten free at the project. When he finally asked the kitchen they let him know they did have some pre made gluten free corn tortillas on hand that they could use to make a taco. It always is odd to me when restaurants make corn tortillas which are traditionally gluten free with gluten, this should be more clearly identified on a menu and staff should be more knowledgeable and willing to accommodate. 

Once we finally got through the pain of ordering with our waiter we got our appetizer. We ordered the "avocado" which we assumed would be chips and guac. It was a little different but was delicious! The avocado dip had some sort of different season in it which made it delightful, would definitely recommend this! 

As for the tacos, we all thought the old project menu had better options and decided we'd prefer to just get the tacos at corazon as we thought they are ultimately better.

Love the fun vibe of the project, but we'll keep going to Corazon at public market where they have everything down to an art and customer service seems to be be more on par.

Went here for dinner and had the steak and fries, as well as the mussels and clams. The steak had a chimichurri sauce that really overpowered the whole plate. I left most of it because of the overpowering taste, and it was not tender. The mussels and clams were pretty good, but not great (maybe a 3.5 out of 5 review, for that plate). The restaurant wasn't too busy and we never got a water refill. 2 stars for the pricey chewy steak  and subpar service.
This was exceptional Mexican food. Wonderful, complex flavors that I never experienced before. A real treat.

review_info.review_text:
Wanted to have a great experience here when they reopened but it was pretty ok. 

We arrived and we're seated quickly which was great and they accommodated getting us in a spot where a baby car seat could easily fit next to our table outside. 

The menu seems to be a lot smaller and different than the previous menu at the project which we were bummed about. 

When our waiter first came over I let them know I had a few dietary restrictions, he seemed unsure about how to answer my questions so bc of his uncertainties he just said I shouldn't order basically anything. When I asked him to check with the kitchen he initially said no. After much pressing on this he finally went back and asked. I learned that the blue corn tortillas (which are gluten free at corazon) are not gluten free at the project. When he finally asked the kitchen they let him know they did have some pre made gluten free corn tortillas on hand that they could use to make a taco. It always is odd to me when restaurants make corn tortillas which are traditionally gluten free with gluten, this should be more clearly identified on a menu and staff should be more knowledgeable and willing to accommodate. 

Once we finally got through the pain of ordering with our waiter we got our appetizer. We ordered the "avocado" which we assumed would be chips and guac. It was a little different but was delicious! The avocado dip had some sort of different season in it which made it delightful, would definitely recommend this! 

As for the tacos, we all thought the old project menu had better options and decided we'd prefer to just get the tacos at corazon as we thought they are ultimately better.

Love the fun vibe of the project, but we'll keep going to Corazon at public market where they have everything down to an art and customer service seems to be be more on par.

Went here for dinner and had the steak and fries, as well as the mussels and clams. The steak had a chimichurri sauce that really overpowered the whole plate. I left most of it because of the overpowering taste, and it was not tender. The mussels and clams were pretty good, but not great (maybe a 3.5 out of 5 review, for that plate). The restaurant wasn't too busy and we never got a water refill. 2 stars for the pricey chewy steak  and subpar service.
This was exceptional Mexican food. Wonderful, complex flavors that I never experienced before. A real treat.

I'm not vegan and this place was great, delicious and super satisfying.

I had the avocado burger, and my friend had the kale burger.  We order a Brussels sprouts side, but the burgers are so plentiful we couldn't eat it all. We left feeling satisfied but not weighed down. 

The guys working were really nice, and service was fast.  

We ended up eating at the market because it wasn't very crowded and it was just an over all great experience.

I love a good falafel sandwich. This was Top Notch! I ordered two spicy Falafel sandwiches. (I had one a couple days ago and zipped back for a repeat order. The falafel was actually spicy (vs salty spicy and spicy for wimps). It was crunchy in the outside and tender on the inside. The veg mix was super spot on! The extra hot sauce was freaking amazing and I emptied it! Tahini sauce was as perfect as could be. I might just revisit one more time before we leave SB. Sorry for not sharing pics; I didn't take the time away from my amazing lunch!
Kale falafel burger was absolutely incredible. I've never really actively sought out vegan food, but this has made me start rethinking that. Super great flavor, and so nice to look at!

review_info.review_text: Recently tried this place twice. Both times the food was excellent. Great super fresh and authentic choices at a reasonable price. My new favorite Mexican take-out!

This hole in the wall in the middle of Old Town Goleta has a great carnitas burrito. The carnitas is as good as the carnitas Rubio's used to have. At this point in my food journey, that's worth 5 stars. And it's not one of those half beans burritos. It does have some high quality beans, but also a small medley of well-seasoned veggie type ingredients. 

There is also no need to even consider the jumbo unless you brought a wagon to wheel that thing home - and you probably want to eat it at home or Goleta Beach because there isn't any seating thanks to Covid. Even when the dining room was open, it never seemed like there were that many people in there. That said, the couple who runs the place is very nice, the prices are downright cheap, and if you haven't heard, they have a great carnitas burrito.

I got the giant meat quesadilla and it was great! You can choose a kind of meat out of a big list with all the same price. Good combination of guac, sour cream and just a right amount of cheese. I will definitely come back and try other menu but I really liked the quesadilla that I would order it again with another choice of meat. Nice family restaurant with friendly people.

I do not think that a lot of people know about this karaoke place. This place also sell boba tea drinks as well. I stayed at the place to almost closing. The worker there was very nice in that she did not try to rush me out of the room since I was the only one there.

The 2nd time that I went there was when I reserved the small room for 3 people. The female coworker, who could have been the owner, was very nice to give us the medium sized room with no additional charge. The private karaoke rooms were very cute with the Hello Kitty Decorations. The sound system was good and the English song choices were enough to keep my friends and I entertained. We could have been there for a few more hours if we were not charged by the hour.

UPDATE: My friends and I were looking forward to going on a Friday night and we finally found a time that was suitable for all of us. Even after Yelp and google both told us they were open at 7pm on a Friday evening, they were closed with no explanation. We even tried calling but they seemed to hang up after I got through. We were really disappointed that we drove all the way there and met up and some of us even canceled previous plans to go to karaoke just to find out that they were closed.


This is usually our go-to place for karaoke in Santa Barbara because it's the only room-style karaoke but the drinks and milk tea are lacking. For karaoke it is a good place to go with a big group of friends and just rent out a room. The rooms are not completely sound proof but who cares when you're having fun with friends. The only downside would be that some songs are hard to find with their system and they don't have any korean or Japanese songs that we could find. Other than that, it's a pretty good place for karaoke.

review_info.review_text: Came here for boba a few times, and while it is pretty good the boba can also be unpredictable. I've gone a few times and the boba was perfectly cooked, and a few other times it was too soft. Still a great option for boba in SB!

I enjoyed my time at this karaoke place last year either in September or October. I came to this place because I wanted to treat a friend out to some Asian style karaoke who lived in Central California. This place was the closest that I saw that was between Southern and Central California. The first time that I came there was by myself. I was the only one who used the karaoke room. I do not think that a lot of people know about this karaoke place. This place also sell boba tea drinks as well. I stayed at the place to almost closing. The worker there was very nice in that she did not try to rush me out of the room since I was the only one there.

The 2nd time that I went there was when I reserved the small room for 3 people. The female coworker, who could have been the owner, was very nice to give us the medium sized room with no additional charge. The private karaoke rooms were very cute with the Hello Kitty Decorations. The sound system was good and the English song choices were enough to keep my friends and I entertained. We could have been there for a few more hours if we were not charged by the hour.

UPDATE: My friends and I were looking forward to going on a Friday night and we finally found a time that was suitable for all of us. Even after Yelp and google both told us they were open at 7pm on a Friday evening, they were closed with no explanation. We even tried calling but they seemed to hang up after I got through. We were really disappointed that we drove all the way there and met up and some of us even canceled previous plans to go to karaoke just to find out that they were closed.


This is usually our go-to place for karaoke in Santa Barbara because it's the only room-style karaoke but the drinks and milk tea are lacking. For karaoke it is a good place to go with a big group of friends and just rent out a room. The rooms are not completely sound proof but who cares when you're having fun with friends. The only downside would be that some songs are hard to find with their system and they don't have any korean or Japanese songs that we could find. Other than that, it's a pretty good place for karaoke.

My boyfriend and I have been here a few times and it's always a great experience! COVID is tough on businesses these days and changes aren't always the best. We were skeptical paying at the counter since service typically suffers that way, but not here. Our server Riley was so hospitable and anticipated our needs before we could even ask. We had a few mimosas and had ZERO trouble getting another round thanks to Riley's impeccable service. He made the end of our trip a pleasant one! 

Onto the food: my boyfriend ordered the Presidio Burrito (he's tried it twice) which was delicious. It was generously filled with chorizo, home fries, cheddar and jack cheese, avocado, and salsa. It's paired with a side salad that's pretty tasty as well. For myself, I tried the Salmon Benny that was paired with a side of home fries. The entree was good, but the burritos here are definitely better. 

Drinks: this establishment has pretty good coffee whatever brand they use. Flavored creamer isn't necessary. We also had a few rounds of mimosas which are pretty darn good for $6 apiece. They have a variety of flavors to choose from too - peach, guava, pomegranate, pineapple and mango (my favorite). 

If you're in SB, definitely give this place a try. Your tummy will thank you.

We really wanted to like this place, but it fell sorta flat.  While the server was very nice, the food not so much.  For the price, the chicken panini was small and basic.  Flavor was something I could have made at home.  Same for the salad.  It was a very small portion of salad greens.  I also ordered the Sausage Kale soup.  It smelled great, but since we eat with our eyes first, I could not get past the layer of thick floating grease/oil on the top. I could not eat it.  That layer of fat needs to be removed.  I understand fat is flavor, but this was too much.

Briefly answer the following question:
how to freeze hash browns
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Place cubed hash browns in moisture-and air-proof containers such as rigid plastic freezer containers or resealable plastic bags. To freeze grated hash browns, place the frozen hash brown patties in a plastic freezer container or resealable bag.To simplify serving, put a piece of freezer wrap between each patty or wrap each patty in an individual resealable bag.rated Hash Browns. To freeze grated hash browns, boil whole, clean potatoes in the jackets until the potatoes are almost done but still firm. When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, they are ready to peel and grate.

passage 2:Freezing Potatoes for Hash Browns. To freeze potatoes for hash browns, shred potatoes; hold in a bowl of cold water until all potatoes are shredded. Drain and blanch in boiling water about 3 minutes.Drain, rinse in cold water, drain again and pat dry. Pack into freezer containers or resealable bags.lanch in boiling water for 2 minutes; plunge into cold water; drain and dry well with paper towels. Fry in hot oil (375°) until very light brown. Drain on paper towels until cool. Pack into freezer containers or bags. Later, fry frozen potatoes in deep fat preheated to 375° until crisp and golden brown.

To freeze them, lay them flat on a parchment paper lined cookie sheet. Put the cookie sheet into the freezer for a couple of hours or until the potatoes are frozen, then transfer them into freezer bags to cook up when you’re ready.

output:
response: To freeze hash browns, first shred or cube potatoes. If you're shredding, hold the shredded potatoes in a bowl of cold water until all are shredded. If freezing patties, put a piece of freezer wrap between each patty or wrap each patty in an individual resealable bag. For shredded hash browns, you can also lay them flat on a parchment paper lined cookie sheet and freeze until they're hard, then transfer them into freezer bags.

smell in a house how to get rid of
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:When these critters grow in number, they can generate a pretty strong odor. They can even spread to other regions of your home, which strengthens the musty scent. The culprits are molds and mildew, which thrive in organic materials.

passage 2:Clean your home thoroughly using a strong cleaning solution and cleaning rags. Pay attention to places you don't normally clean, such as inside cabinets, under sinks and along window sills. Wipe down the walls, baseboards, doors and counter tops with a 1 to 10 solution of bleach and water. Air out each room by opening the windows. Choose a nice day with a breeze to help move air throughout your home. Airing out the rooms will help release odors in curtains, carpets and furniture. Keep the windows open for at least an hour, or longer for particularly heavy odors.

passage 3:While this won't get rid of the smell, it'll help. Also, set bowls of white vinegar around your home, at least one per room (depending on the room size). Just make sure small children and pets are safe. If you have an air purifier or can borrow one or two from friends, this is a great way to decrease smoke smell. It takes time for the air to become clean, so I suggest keeping the purifier in the room you use the most. In the day, that might be the kitchen or home office. At night, the bedroom.

source_text:
Briefly answer the following question:
risks benefits roth ira vs 401k
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:A Roth 401(k) account works much like a Roth IRA, but there is no income limit to participate, and you are required to take the minimum distributions that would be required from a Traditional IRA beginning at age 70½.There is also a Roth version of the 403(b) plan.gain, if you're able to save more after you put $5,500 in a Roth, continue with your 401(k) until you max it out. 1  If you're not eligible for either a deductible contribution to a traditional IRA or a Roth IRA contribution, then just continue with your 401(k) until you've contributed the maximum allowed.

passage 2:Contribution Limits. You can contribute up to $18,000/year to your Roth 401(k), as well as an additional $6,000 if you'll turn 50 by the end of the year. That number is much lower for Roth IRAs, which limit you to $5,500 a year or $6,500 if you're 50 or older. Here, the Roth 401(k) is the clear winner.or example, if you have both a Roth IRA and Roth 401(k) – and you're eligible to make contributions to both – your annual contribution maximum effectively becomes $23,500 (or $30,500 if you're 50 or older). This round goes to the Roth IRA.

passage 3:Another risk with Roth IRAs is that unlike a 401(k) , the IRS, not your employer, places limits on how much you can put into your retirement fund.You cannot contribute more than you make to your fund, and if you make too much money, you cannot open a Roth IRA.he main risk for opening a Roth IRA is that you do not get the same up-front tax break you get with a traditional IRA. A traditional IRA lets you put money aside before taxes, but the money you put into your Roth IRA goes into your account after your taxes are taken.

It also offers higher contribution limits, $18,000/year plus an additional $6,000 if you're 50 or older. By comparison, Roth IRAs limit contributions to $5,500 a year, or $6,500 if you're 50 or older. However, a risk of Roth IRAs is that the IRS places limits on how much you can contribute and if you make too much money, you cannot open a Roth IRA. Additionally, unlike a traditional IRA which allows for pre-tax contributions, Roth IRA contributions are post-tax, so there is no immediate tax deduction.

source_text:
Briefly answer the following question:
how to check a temperature gauge
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Main Features. 1  Reads temperature information from all Intel Core based processors. 2  Ability to individually calibrate Real Temp for each core of your CPU. 3  Program is based on temperature data gathered using a Fluke 62 IR Thermometer.  Test Sensors feature will check your DTS sensors for any sign of problems.

passage 2:With the ignition on and the engine not running, disconnect the gauge wire (yellow with red stripe) from the sending unit in the coolant outlet on the cylinder head. On 16-valve engines, the sending unit is on the driver's-side end of the cylinder head. Ground the wire. This simulates a high engine temperature signal to the gauge. If the gauge needle moves upward, the sending unit is faulty and should be replaced. If the needle still does not move, either the wire to the gauge is broken (open circuit) or the gauge is faulty.

passage 3:While the gauge is unplugged from the sender, it is not uncommon for it to register temperature in the 110 to 140 degrees F range. If the resistance measured matched the gauge reading, the problem will likely either be the sender, or that the engine really is running the temperature that your gauge is displaying.

In case the passages do not contain the necessary information to answer the question, please reply with: "Unable to answer based on given passages."

Disconnect the gauge wire from the sending unit in the coolant outlet on the cylinder head. Ground the wire, which simulates a high engine temperature signal to the gauge. If the gauge needle moves upward, the sending unit is faulty and should be replaced. If the needle does not move, either the wire to the gauge is broken or the gauge is faulty. If the gauge is unplugged from the sender and it registers temperature in the 110 to 140 degrees F range, and the resistance measured matches the gauge reading, the problem could either be the sender, or that the engine is actually running the temperature that your gauge is displaying. Briefly answer the following question:
how to barbecue asparagus in foil
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:On gas grills, set the heat to medium. On charcoal grills, set the asparagus away from the center. You'll want to grill for about five minutes. Regardless of where you're grilling your asparagus, if it's not wrapped in foil (so you can't see) be sure to keep an eye on it.

passage 2:Tear off a piece of foil about twice as long as it is wide. Toss the asparagus with oil and any spices you'd like to add, and then lay it on the foil in a single layer. Fold the foil over the top, and crimp the edges. Lay the packet on the grill (to the side, not over the very center) and cook for about five minutes.

passage 3:Preheat grill to a medium flame. While grill is preheating, clean asparagus, chop the ends off. 2. Take a large sheet of tinfoil, and place the asparagus in the middle of it. Gather the sides together and then bring the tops together. Don’t seal just yet. Add your olive oil, garlic, and salt and pepper. Close the pouch and gently shake, so that everything is incorporated. Peak back in the pouch to make sure the asparagus is covered with a smidge of olive oil. If not add a little more (eyeball it). 3. Add the pouch to direct heat on a grill for about 20 minutes.

spicy pineapple shrimp stir fry
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Shrimp and Pineapple Stir-fry. 1  Whisk together sauce ingredients and set aside. 2  Heat 2 teaspoons sesame oil and 1/2 tablespoon vegetable oil in large non-stick skillet on medium-high until shimmering hot. 3  Add pineapple to skillet and stir-fry until lightly browned. Remove pineapple to a bowl. Add shrimp and garlic to skillet. Cook 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove shrimp and garlic to the bowl with pineapple. Add remaining oil to skillet and heat until shimmering. Add bell pepper, bok choy, asparagus, carrots, and sugar snap peas to skillet.

passage 2:Hot cooked rice. Drain pineapple, reserving juice. In a small bowl, mix cornstarch, broth, brown sugar, orange juice, soy sauce and reserved pineapple juice until smooth. In a large skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add peppers and onion; stir-fry 1-2 minutes or just until crisp-tender. Add shrimp; stir-fry 2-3 minutes longer or until shrimp turn pink. Remove from pan. Place pineapple in skillet. Stir cornstarch mixture and add to pan. Bring to a boil; cook and stir 4-5 minutes or until sauce is thickened. Return shrimp mixture to pan; heat through, stirring to combine. Sprinkle with coconut; serve with rice. Yield: 4 servings.

Briefly answer the following question:
what is the difference between communicable and non communicable diseases
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Communicable disease refers to diseases that can pass from one person to another. Non-communicable diseases occur in one person and cannot be passed on to another person. Communicable diseases are also known as infectious diseases, and non-communicable diseases are referred to as chronic.

passage 2:One important difference between communicable and non-communicable disease is that non-communicable diseases tend to be chronic, which means they last a long time and progress slowly. Communicable diseases are more likely to be acute, which means the disease develops quickly.

passage 3:Cancers are one category of non-communicable diseases that cannot be spread to others. Chicken pox and other conditions caused by viruses are communicable diseases. Non-infectious diseases involving the respiratory system are a class of non-communicable conditions.

In case the passages do not contain the necessary information to answer the question, please reply with: "Unable to answer based on given passages."

response: Communicable diseases are those that can pass from one person to another, also known as infectious diseases. They are more likely to be acute, meaning they develop quickly. Examples include conditions caused by viruses such as chicken pox. On the other hand, non-communicable diseases are those that occur in one person and cannot be passed on to another. They are also referred to as chronic diseases because they tend to last a long time and progress slowly. Examples include cancers and non-infectious diseases involving the respiratory system.

how to make potato leek soup

passage 1:Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy soup pot over medium heat and add the onion, leeks and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until tender, about 5 minutes. Uncover, and add remaining potatoes, bouquet garni, salt, pepper, chicken stock and cream. Stir. Bring the soup to a simmer over medium heat, uncovered.

response: To make a poached egg, fill a wide, shallow saucepan or skillet with 2-3 inches of water and bring it to a simmer over medium to medium-high heat. You will see bubbles around the edges of the pan and under the surface but not on the surface. Using a large spoon, dip the whole eggs under the water for 15 seconds. Then, carefully drop the egg into the center of a whirlpool created in the pan. The swirling water will help prevent the egg white from spreading out in the pan. Turn off the heat, cover the pan and let it poach for 5 minutes without peeking, poking, stirring or accosting the egg in any way. After 5 minutes, remove the egg with a slotted spoon and serve immediately. If not serving immediately, transfer the egg to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking process and refrigerate up to 8 hours. To reheat, slide eggs into gently simmering water until warmed through, for about 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, and remove with a slotted spoon.

Briefly answer the following question:
how does a flat screen tv work
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:The set-up. Housed between two sheets of glass is the technology that allows flat screen TVs to work. Depending on the type of flat screen TV, the process can differ slightly. In a plasma TVs are cells that contain the gases xenon and neon as well as electrodes.There are two types of electrodes, display and address, that are arranged in a grid-like pattern on either side of the cells.n a LCD flat screen TV, tiny liquid-crystal-filled cells are between the glass sheets. A bright white light is located behind the cells and illuminates them to create the picture.

passage 2:Like said earlier, a LED TV is an enhanced and improved version of a LCD TV. LED TVs have slimmer and thinner body panel. The back-light intensity and brightness is much more. Pixel clarity is fine and clear. The baseline functioning of LED is that it illuminates the LCD panels by using LED technology.his chemical is what makes the pixels red, green, or blue. When the plasma TV is electronically turned on, the electricity causes the colored phosphors to produce light. This in turn paints the moving pictures on the screen. For more information on plasma televisions, read How a Plasma TV Works.

passage 3:Powering the picture. The power supply enters the TV and creates the energy needed to create the picture. In a plasma TV, electric pulses excite the gases, which produce release ultraviolet photons. These photons react with the phosphor material that is contained in the cells. how does a snorkel work underwater
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Answer Wiki. 3 Answers. , Emphasizes the second syllable in cannibal. When the batteries need to be recharged, but the submarine wants to reduce its exposure to surface detection, it gets to a shallow depth and raises the snorkel. Most notably, the snorkel is for the diesel engine itself, not the crew.

passage 2:Best Value Snorkel And Mask Combo. If you also need a mask for snorkeling, Cressi offers a great deal on a mask and dry snorkel set. This set has earned a solid 4.5/5.0 rating and has almost 600 reviews. The mask is a low volume mask with a silicone skirt and gives a great field of vision.

passage 3:Part 2: How do Dry Snorkels Work? Dry snorkels have a mechanism at the top of the tube that closes when you submerge under water. It also has a covering at the top to prevent surface water from splashing into the top of tube. The dry snorkel has a valve/hinge mechanism at the top. When you submerge underwater, accidentally or purposely, the hinge reacts via a float mechanism and closes onto the top of the tube and seals it which prevents water from filling the tube.

In case the passages do not contain the necessary information to answer the question, please reply with: "Unable to answer based on given passages."
output:
response: Dry snorkels work underwater through a mechanism at the top of the tube that closes when submerged. This mechanism prevents water from filling the tube. There is also a covering at the top to prevent surface water from splashing into the tube. When the user submerges underwater, either accidentally or purposely, a valve/hinge mechanism reacts via a float mechanism, closing onto the top of the tube and sealing it. This design is meant to keep the snorkel dry even when underwater.

symptoms of raynaud's disease

passage 2:Symptoms of Raynaud’s Syndrome. 1) Fingers start to go white as the circulation is restricted in the capillaries. Whiteness can be on just one or just part of one finger, or two or three fingers at a time. Often there are patches of white, showing a mottled appearance. 2) Affected areas will feel numb and have a white waxy look. 3) Symptoms can often include the affected areas going blue or showing a bluish tinge. This is due to a lack of oxygen in the red blood cells. 4) As the episode ends, affected areas will go bright red as the fresh oxygenated blood returns to the capillaries and cells. 4) As the circulation is restored to the attacked areas, one can experience tingling and pain and may feel like pins and needles.

passage 3:Secondary Raynaud's can occur due a connective tissue disorder such as scleroderma or lupus, injuries to the hands, smoking, and certain medications such as birth control pills. Diagnosis is typically based on the symptoms.

what is the difference between ravens and crows
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Physical Differences. Crows and ravens differ physically from one another, their size being the most noticeable. Ravens are larger than crows, making them the largest perching birds. Crows have a smooth texture whereas the raven has a dense and shaggy plumage particularly around the throat. The bill of the raven is also heavier than the crow's bill. During flight, the spreading of the tail can distinguish the crow and raven apart. The tail of the crow spreads into a fan-like structure while the tail of the raven spreads into a wedge shape.

passage 2:Difference between Crows and Ravens. Crows and ravens are birds of the Corvidae family that are mainly renowned for their intelligence in tool use, enemy identification, problem solving and mimicry.

passage 3:Telling the birds apart if they are seen together is a simple matter, as the size difference between the species will be obvious. It is not always possible to determine whether a large, black corvid is an American crow or a common raven, but using different opportunities to try can be a great chance to sharpen your bird identification skills.

The tail of a crow spreads into a fan-like structure during flight, while the tail of a raven spreads into a wedge shape. Both species are known for their intelligence, including tool use, enemy identification, problem-solving, and mimicry. The size difference between the two is usually noticeable when they are seen together.

centralized vs decentralized government definition

All the important decision and actions at the lower level, all subjects and actions at the lower level are subject to the approval of top management.ecentralization is not the same as delegation. In fact, decentralization is all extension of delegation. Decentralization pattern is wider is scope and the authorities are diffused to the lowest most level of management. Delegation of authority is a complete process and takes place from one person to another.

Other types of bonds include metallic bonds and hydrogen bonding.

Roast. Throw that skillet in the oven for about 10 to 15 minutes more, flipping the tenderloin over halfway through cooking, until the meat reaches 140°F (or, if you don't have a meat thermometer, until it feels firm and springs back when pressed with your finger and the juices run clear when poked with a knife).

passage 3:Let the tenderloin cool before serving. Pan-roasting pork tenderloin Preheat your oven to 425ºF and coat an ovenproof skillet with oil. Sear the tenderloin over medium-high heat until it’s brown on all sides. Roast the tenderloin for 15 to 20 minutes until the internal temperature reads 145ºF.ou can grill it or roast it. Grilling pork tenderloin Always cook the tenderloin over indirect heat. Depending on its size, it usually takes 20 to 30 minutes over medium-high heat. Flip the tenderloin every 4 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 135ºF to 140ºF.

Sprinkle it generously with kosher salt and sugar, then press the crushed peppercorns all over the surface of the meat. Insert a meat thermometer and place in the oven. The beef will probably cook in 20 to 25 minutes depending on its temp before it goes in the oven, and it should register 120 to 125 degrees F on the meat thermometer for medium-rare/rare. Alternatively, you can roast the tenderloin in a skillet in the oven for about 10 to 15 minutes more, flipping it over halfway through cooking, until the meat reaches 140°F, or until it feels firm and springs back when pressed with your finger and the juices run clear when poked with a knife. Let the tenderloin cool before serving.

1. Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F.
2. Place the tenderloin on a roasting rack.
3. Sprinkle generously with kosher salt and sugar.

Briefly answer the following question:
what is the difference between quality assurance and quality control
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:As such, it is normally good to think of these two terms as logical phases in the general process of delivering something valuable to the end users. passage 2:Quality Control is focused on the initiation of the evaluation process, while quality assurance is focused on managing the process to ensure the stipulated business goals are realized within the set period of time.

passage 3:In general, the QA activities are done before the product is manufactured or the service delivered (proactive approach). The QC activities are done during the manufacturing process and once the product is manufactured. QA is process oriented. QC is product oriented.

output:

QA is a proactive process that starts with defining procedures, rules, and policies for selecting and using raw materials in the manufacturing process. It is focused on managing the process to ensure that business goals are met within a set period of time. On the other hand, QC is focused on the evaluation process and takes place during and after the manufacturing process. It is product-oriented and is aimed at ensuring the quality of the finished product.

passage 1:Home treatments may be advised for mild, viral meningitis. Medications for headaches, pain killers, and anti-sickness drugs to prevent vomiting are enough for the patient to recover within 14 days. There s no need to continue taking antibiotics once viral meningitis is confirmed.

passage 2:Avoid Liquid Food: When you get diagnosed with meningitis, the patients should avoid liquid food. Instead of that food, they should drink the juice of ORS (oral re-hydration salts). The better way on how to treat meningitis naturally is to mix the juice of ORS with the lukewarm water. This is the treatment for the first days.

passage 3:1. Take A Good Sleep: As the way on how to treat meningitis, the doctors have suggested that the patients with meningitis need to take a good sleep for at least 8 hours a day. By putting the patients into the comfortable bed rest, this treatment will help them relieve the symptoms of meningitis such as headache.

To eat a sweet baked potato, follow these steps:

1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
2. Prick your sweet potatoes several times with a fork and place them directly on the oven rack, above the foil.
3. Bake the sweet potatoes for 45 minutes or until they are tender when poked with a fork.
4. Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and let them cool slightly.
5. Cut the sweet potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a thin layer to hold the shape of the potato.
6. In a small bowl, mix together softened butter, real maple syrup, chopped pecans, and vanilla extract.
7. Spread the mixture onto the hollowed-out sweet potato skins.
8. Place the sweet potato skins back into the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes or until the filling is golden brown.
9. Serve warm and enjoy!

how can o you tell when a person has alcohol poisoning
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:An overdose of alcohol occurs when a person has a blood alcohol content (or BAC) sufficient to produce impairments that increase the risk of harm. Overdoses can range in severity, from problems with balance and slurred speech to coma or even death.

passage 2:If you suspect that someone has alcohol poisoning, even if you don’t see the classic signs and symptoms, seek immediate medical care. In an emergency, follow these suggestions 1  : If the person is unconscious, breathing less than eight times a minute or has repeated, uncontrolled vomiting, call 911 immediately.

passage 3:Alcohol poisoning signs and symptoms include: 1  Confusion. 2  Vomiting. 3  Seizures. 4  Slow breathing (less than eight breaths a minute). 5  Irregular breathing (a gap of more than 10 seconds between breaths). 6  Blue-tinged skin or pale skin. 7  Low body temperature (hypothermia).

In case the passages do not contain the necessary information to answer the question, please reply with: "Unable to answer based on given passages."
output:
response:
Based on the given passages, here are some ways to determine if a person may have alcohol poisoning:

1. Confusion
2. Vomiting
3. Seizures
4. Slow breathing (less than eight breaths a minute)
5. Irregular breathing (a gap of more than 10 seconds between breaths)
6. Blue-tinged skin or pale skin
7. Low body temperature (hypothermia)

If you suspect someone has alcohol poisoning, it's important to seek immediate medical care, even if they don't show all of these signs and symptoms. Call 911 or your local emergency number right away if the person is unconscious, breathing less than eight times a minute, or has repeated, uncontrolled vomiting.

source_text:
Briefly answer the following question:
how to level mailbox post
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Then come back and slide the cast stone post over top of the 4×4 wood post. The front of the cast stone post will lay flat against the front of the 4×4 post. This way, when you screw in the mailbox holder and mailbox to the front of the cast stone post, it will join the two together making the post sturdy.

passage 2:According to standard postal service codes, a mailbox should not sit any higher than 45 inches from street level. Place the post in the hole. Level it and attach two support beams at the center to keep the post standing up straight. Place one at the side of the post, and then add another to the back. This will ensure the post does not move while pouring the concrete and it remains level while the concrete is drying. Pour the dry concrete straight into the hole leaving 3 to 4 inches of space from the top of the hole.

passage 3:1. Use shovel or posthole digger to dig a hole for the mailbox post; place dirt onto a tarp. 2. Keep in mind that bottom of mailbox must be 41 to 45 inches above street, and front of mailbox must be no more than 8 inches from curb. 3. Set mailbox post in hole and use a post level to hold it perfectly plumb. 4. Backfill around the post with 10 or 12 inches of soil. 5. Use a sledgehammer or long 2x4 to tamp down the soil around the post. 6. Add a little more soil and tamp again; repeat until hole is completely filled. 7. Remove the post level and attach the diagonal brace with galvanized decking screws. 8. Attach the mailbox to the post with galvanized decking screws.

output:
response: To level a mailbox post, first dig a hole for the post using a shovel or posthole digger. The bottom of the mailbox should be 41 to 45 inches above street level, and the front of the mailbox should not be more than 8 inches from the curb. Set the mailbox post in the hole and use a post level to hold it perfectly plumb. Backfill around the post with soil and tamp it down with a sledgehammer or a long 2x4. Add more soil and tamp again until the hole is completely filled. Attach two support beams at the center to keep the post upright, one at the side and another at the back. Pour dry concrete into the hole, leaving 3 to 4 inches from the top. This will ensure the post does not move while the concrete is drying and remains level. When the concrete has dried, slide the cast stone post over the wooden post. Attach the mailbox to the post with galvanized decking screws.

Briefly answer the following question:
how to relieve tight calf muscles
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Treatment for Tight Calf Muscles: If a calf cramp or tightness strikes in the middle of a run, stretching the muscle is the best immediate fix. Find a curb and rest the forefoot of the leg that's cramping on the curb. Slowly lower your heel off the curb and hold for 30 seconds. If your calf really starts seizing up, you may need to gently massage the area. After runs, one of the best ways to treat tight calf muscles is to see a sports massage therapist or physical therapist for a deep tissue massage. If you don't have the money or time for professional massages, you can also do self-massage at home using a massage tool such as a massage ball or foam roller.

passage 2:Perform calf raises by first standing with your hands holding the back of a chair or table. Slowly raise your heels off the ground so that you are standing on your toes and the balls of your feet. You should feel a stretch in your calf muscles. Hold this position for a few seconds. Relax and repeat.

passage 3:Calf Stretch Tips: 1  Hold Time: Work up to holding each stretch for 20 seconds or more. 2  Set Count: Three to five sets of holding a stretch, per leg.  Breathe: Slowly inhale through your nose and exhale out your mouth during each stretch.

Briefly answer the following question:
how to add a paid stamp in quickbooks
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Look for your invoice template that you are using, highlight it, right click on your mouse and Edit Template. This will open up the Basic Customization screen. Let your eyes scan to the bottom section of that page called Company & Transaction Information, and you will see a box that says beside it – Print Status Stamp.Clicking on that box will make a check mark which will then activate that Status Stamp to be printed when it has been PAID.If you email an invoice that has been paid, then that PAID stamp will appear in the PDF document that QuickBooks sends. And that’s how you get the PAID stamp to appear on a paid invoice.Note: www.quickbookstrained.com is now mobile friendly.From the web address you can choose Options/Mobile formatted and the site will appear in all its living colour for you to view. Check it out.et your eyes scan to the bottom section of that page called Company & Transaction Information, and you will see a box that says beside it – Print Status Stamp. Clicking on that box will make a check mark which will then activate that Status Stamp to be printed when it has been PAID.

passage 2:Modify a Template. Before you void the invoice you need to create your template. Click the customize manage templates button. Click the Copy button to make a copy of the template, then change the template name to “Void Invoice” in the Template Name box.Click “OK” to close the window. Un-check the Print Status Stamp box, then click Additional Customization.lick the customize manage templates button. Click the Copy button to make a copy of the template, then change the template name to “Void Invoice” in the Template Name box. Click “OK” to close the window.

output:
response: To add a paid stamp in Quickbooks, you need to find the invoice template you are using, highlight it, then right click and choose Edit Template. This will open up the Basic Customization screen. From there, look for the section at the bottom called Company & Transaction Information. Within this section, there's a box next to the words Print Status Stamp. Clicking on this box will add a check mark, which activates the status stamp to be printed when the invoice has been paid. If you email an invoice that has been paid, the PAID stamp will appear in the PDF document that QuickBooks sends.

Briefly answer the following question:
how to grow healthy tomatoes in a container
Bear in mind that your response should be strictly based on the following three passages:
passage 1:Transplanting Tips for Container Tomatoes. * A 5-gallon container is perfect for the tomato and easy to move if needed. * Clay pots tend to dry out quickly unless they are glazed or painted. * Drill multiple 1/4 inch holes in the bottom of the tomato container. Don’t try to get by with just one drainage hole. * Place 2 to 3 inches of gravel in the bottom for drainage. * Fill the container about 3/4 full with bagged potting soil to start. As the container tomato baby grows bigger, add fresh soil to the top to support the growing stem. * Plant 3 or 4 marigolds with each tomato to help keep bugs away. * Container tomatoes should receive full sun (about 8 hours a day).

passage 2:The hotter the temperature and the smaller the container, the more watering you will have to do. Mulch can help conserve soil moisture. While you are checking your containers for water, keep an eye out for insects and diseases. The same pests bother tomatoes whether you grow the plants in the ground or in containers.

passage 3:To avoid damaging the plants put the supports in the containers before you plant the seedlings. Fill each container three-quarters full. Plant each seedling so the soil is just below the first set of true leaves, which are the leaves that look like tomato leaves. Firm the soil around each plant, then water thoroughly.

Place 2 to 3 inches of gravel at the bottom, then fill it three-quarters full with bagged potting soil. Transplant the seedling so that the soil is just below the first set of true leaves, then firm the soil around each plant and water thoroughly. As the tomato plant grows, add fresh soil to support the growing stem. Plant 3 or 4 marigolds with each tomato plant to help keep bugs away. Place the container in full sun, where it can receive around 8 hours of light a day. Regularly check the containers for water, insects, and diseases. The hotter the temperature and the smaller the container, the more frequent the watering. Mulch can be used to conserve soil moisture.
